items.title: Hong Kong: Joshua Wong Gets Nearly 10 More Years in Prison
items.description: Click to expand Image Joshua Wong speaks to protesters near the Legislative Council in Hong Kong, June 17, 2019. © 2019 Kin Cheung/AP Photo (Tokyo) – The Hong Kong High Court on November 5, 2026, sentenced Joshua Wong, a well-known democracy activist, to 10 years in prison on baseless national security charges, Human Rights Watch said today. Two months of the sentence will run concurrently with his current national security sentence. Wong has been in custody since November 2020, when he was 24, and faces imprisonment until late 2036, when he will be 40. The Hong Kong government should immediately and unconditionally release Wong. Foreign governments should denounce the sentences against him and other wrongfully detained pro-democracy activists and impose targeted sanctions on officials responsible for Hong Kong’s growing repression. “The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars.” To keep Hong Kong society subdued, and to reduce the chance of an international outcry, the Hong Kong government appears to have adopted the tactic of stacking charges against influential pro-democracy leaders to ensure their prolonged detention, Human Rights Watch said. Other notable Hong Kong figures who have faced similar tactics include Jimmy Lai, founder of Apple Daily, and veteran democracy activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Albert Ho. The court sentenced Wong, 30, under the National Security Law for “conspiring to collude with foreign forces.” The authorities accused him of “conspiring” with the activist Nathan Law and other “unknown” individuals between 2016 and November 2020 to urge foreign governments to sanction Hong Kong and Chinese government officials as they advocated for Hong Kong’s “democratic self-determination.” The prosecution relied heavily on the international lobbying and media advocacy that Wong and Demosisto, the political party Wong co-founded in 2016, carried out before the National Security Law took effect. Wong initiated online petitions, spoke to international media, and met with foreign officials to draw attention to human rights abuses in Hong Kong. He urged governments to sanction Chinese and Hong Kong officials responsible for abuses and to stop selling weapons to Hong Kong police that they use to carry out rights violations. Wong had mostly stopped these activities before the National Security Law became effective. Demosisto disbanded on June 30, 2020, and Wong resigned from the group. However, the government quoted social media posts by Wong as ostensible evidence that his alleged “conspiracy” with Law to commit “foreign collusion” continued after the law took effect. In these posts, Wong said he “would not change his views” and that he would “continue to seek support from the international community” in his personal capacity, while Law and others abroad would continue their international advocacy. The government also cited Wong’s subsequent opinion pieces and media interviews, though none directly called for sanctions, which the National Security Law specifically prohibits. It also cited his reposts of Law’s posts broadly calling for sanctions against Chinese officials and Hong Kong police. The court ruled that Wong’s offense was of a “grave nature.” The National Security Law sets prison terms of 3 to 10 years for “foreign collusion,” or 10 years to life for offenses deemed to be of a “grave nature.” Wong formally pleaded guilty on September 2. A guilty plea normally results in a one-third sentence reduction. But a sentence reduction cannot bring the term below the statutory minimum. Because of reporting restrictions on pretrial committal proceedings, when a magistrate determines whether to send a case to a higher court for trial, the public did not know the details of the accusations against Wong until the formal plea. The government enacted a law in 2024 to enable the court, on national security grounds, to deny the defendant’s right to ask the court to lift restrictions on reporting about the case. By restricting media reporting on the pretrial proceedings in national security cases, the government can control the narrative and undermine the fundamental legal principle of open justice. Since Beijing imposed the National Security Law on Hong Kong in June 2020, Hong Kong authorities have used the new legal regime—along with existing laws—to rapidly dismantle civil society and detain, imprison, or force into exile hundreds of activists and government critics. Wong has been in custody since November 2020, when he pleaded guilty to two charges of organizing and inciting an unauthorized assembly linked to the 2019 citywide protest movement. After that, he pleaded guilty to five more charges on separate occasions, including for violating an anti-mask law, participating in an unauthorized vigil for the 1989 Tiananmen Massacre, and breaching a court ban to disclose a police officer’s personal information. While serving these sentences, Wong was charged with two national security offenses, which carry far harsher penalties. In January 2021, Wong was charged with “conspiring to commit subversion” for participating in an unofficial democratic primary in 2020 and sentenced to another four years and eight months in prison. Before Wong could complete these sentences, the authorities brought the “foreign collusion” charge against him in June 2025, ensuring that he would remain in prison. Wong became one of Hong Kong’s best-known democracy activists as a teenager, after leading a massive 2012 protest against a government educational curriculum widely seen as political indoctrination. He became the global face of Hong Kong’s democracy movement during the 2014 Umbrella Movement and co-founded Demosisto with Law and others in 2016. The party disbanded on June 30, 2020, hours before the National Security Law came into effect. The National Security Law’s sweeping provisions have been used to punish peaceful protest and expression. Its use against Wong and others violates the right to freedom of expression under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which is incorporated into Hong Kong law through the city’s de facto constitution, the Basic Law, and the Bill of Rights Ordinance. “Beijing has paid no real price for its increasing repression in Hong Kong,” Pearson said. “Concerned governments should press for the release of Wong and other activists, impose targeted sanctions against implicated officials, and review their relationship with China more broadly in light of the deepening abuses.”

items.title: Mahama says Ghana’s economy remains resilient despite global shocks
items.description: President John Mahama has reassured Ghanaians in the Caribbean that Ghana’s economy remains resilient despite global economic challenges, stressing that key indicators such as inflation, interest rates, and the Cedi are holding steady. Addressing the diaspora Ghanaians in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), the President acknowledged that while 2025 was good and expectations for 2026 were higher, the global economic climate had tempered those hopes, yet Ghana’s economy had remained resilient. “Before, if something like this had happened, our economy would collapse, the Cedi would jump, and inflation would go high. Interest rates would also go high,” the President stated. “But I must say that inflation is holding, interest rates are holding, and the Cedi is holding its own.” President Mahama expressed optimism that after the American mid-term elections, a way would be found to resolve the issues creating the global economic shock, allowing Ghana to continue growing its economy. “So, I think at home, things are okay,” he added. Turning to remittances, the President said his government was working to create more secure investment avenues for diaspora funds. He noted the common practice of sending money to a trusted relative (Wofa)—only to find upon returning home that the funds have disappeared. “We are trying to see how we can make your remittances work better for you. When you come out and you are working, you want to send some money back home. Often, you send that money to a ‘Wofa’ officer or somebody, and then you keep sending money back home. They will be bringing you pictures, and you think everything is okay. Then, when you finish your contract and come back, ‘Wofa’ has disappeared,” he said. The President said the government is therefore exploring more secure ways for diaspora Ghanaians to invest their remittances in ventures that are safer and yield returns. “When you come home, your investment would not have dwindled, but it would have grown. Then you yourself can supervise what you want to invest in,” he assured. He urged diaspora Ghanaians in the Caribbean to take advantage of a $1 billion mortgage initiative designed to help citizens at home and abroad become homeowners. He said housing had become a priority for his administration, with the rollout of a mortgage scheme that will allow beneficiaries to spread payments over 15 to 20 years.

items.title: GBA cautions newly enrolled lawyers against filming court entrances
items.description: The President of the Ghana Bar Association (GBA), Efua Ghartey, has cautioned newly enrolled lawyers against filming their first appearances in court or engaging videographers to record their entry into the courtroom. She warned that the practice is not permitted and could expose lawyers who engage in it to disciplinary action. Speaking at an event, Mrs Ghartey said the association had observed some newly enrolled lawyers recording their first appearances in court. “We’ve seen some people take videos of their fresh legal steps into court. Please, it is not allowed. So please don’t find a videographer to follow you as you enter the courtroom. It is not allowed,” she said. Mrs Ghartey acknowledged the enthusiasm surrounding the entry of new lawyers into the profession but said some had gone beyond acceptable limits. “As seniors, we are enjoying what is going on, but some people have crossed the line, and we don’t want to start calling for disciplinary matters,” she added. Her warning comes amid a growing trend of newly enrolled lawyers documenting their first court appearances, with some sharing the videos on social media. The GBA President urged the new lawyers to respect the professional standards and decorum expected of members of the legal profession, particularly the rules governing conduct within court premises.

items.title: Court admits FG’s evidence against six alleged coup plotters
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday admitted in evidence exhibits tendered by the Federal Government against six persons accused of complicity in an alleged plot to overthrow President Bola Tinubu’s administration through a coup d’état. Among the proof of evidence the court admitted were extrajudicial statements the defendants made before a Special Investigation Panel and military police authorities. Those on trial over the alleged coup are retired Major General Mohammed Ibrahim Gana; retired Naval Captain Erasmus Ochegobia Victor; a serving Police Inspector, Ahmed Ibrahim; and three others: Zekeri Umoru, Bukar Kashim Goni and Abdulkadir Sani. They are answering to a 13-count charge marked FHC/ABJ/CR/206/2026. The defendants had challenged the admissibility of their statements on the premise that they were not made voluntarily but through coercion, in violation of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. The defence lawyers further contended that their clients were denied the right to legal representation during interrogation, insisting there were discrepancies between the video recordings and the defendants’ written statements. Although the prosecution urged the court to dismiss the objections, Justice Joyce Abdulmalik ordered a trial within a trial to ascertain the voluntariness of the extrajudicial statements sought to be tendered. The issue arose while the fourth prosecution witness was testifying. Delivering the ruling on Thursday, Justice Abdulmalik held that the defendants failed to establish their allegation that they were coerced into making confessional statements. The court described the defendants’ claim that they spoke under duress as an afterthought, and it dismissed their allegation of torture. It went ahead to admit both the defendants’ written statements and the video recordings as part of the proof of evidence in the matter. Justice Abdulmalik fixed December 7 and 10 for the continuation of the hearing on the charge. It will be recalled that one of the defendants, Umoru, revealed on May 20 that discussions were held on how the electricity supply to the Presidential Villa, Abuja, would be switched off to aid the alleged coup. Umoru, an employee of Julius Berger Nigeria Plc in the Maintenance Department at the Presidential Villa, made the disclosure in a video recording played in open court. The defendant said he warned that such an action would immediately trigger investigations and the detention of workers on duty. He alleged that the coup’s purported mastermind, Col. Mohammed Ma’aji, offered him money, through the third defendant, Insp. Ibrahim, to recruit between 18 and 19 persons working inside the villa. Umoru said those to be recruited included soldiers, officials of the Department of State Services (DSS) and Julius Berger staff members. He also told investigators that Ma’aji allegedly said he wanted access to the Presidential Villa and could achieve it “with force”, even if those recruited from inside declined to cooperate. Likewise, the sixth defendant, an Islamic cleric, Sheikh Abdulkadir, said in another video recording before the court that he warned the coup plotters that the plan would fail and that they would eventually be exposed. Abdulkadir, a Zaria-based Imam, said he was informed about the plot and recruited to pray against the leakage of information about the activities of those behind it. Timipre Sylva, a former governor of Bayelsa State who also served as Minister of State for Petroleum Resources under the late former President Muhammadu Buhari, was also mentioned in the charge filed by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice. The former governor is said to be at large after fleeing the country before the alleged coup plot was exposed. The allegations against the defendants include treason, terrorism, failure to disclose security intelligence, and money laundering in furtherance of terrorist acts. The FG alleged that the defendants, sometime in September 2025, conspired to levy war against the state to overawe President Tinubu, an offence punishable under Section 37(2) of the Criminal Code. It was further alleged that the defendants had prior knowledge of a planned treasonable act involving Colonel Mohammed Alhassan Ma’aji and others but failed to alert the appropriate authorities. The FG alleged that they rendered assistance to Colonel Ma’aji, as shown by their failure to disclose the coup plot to the president or a peace officer. The defendants were also accused of failing to take preventive steps, having “not used any reasonable endeavours to prevent the commission of the offence.” Other allegations centred on terrorism-related offences under the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. The defendants were said to have conspired to commit an act of terrorism in Nigeria. However, upon their arraignment before the court on April 22, the defendants pleaded not guilty to the charge and were remanded in the custody of the DSS pending determination of the case. The court earlier granted the FG permission to shield the identities of witnesses from the Nigerian Army owing to the sensitive nature of the case. The FG had also produced three bank officials who tendered financial documents in evidence, including letters obtained from the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). items.title: Prophet John Anokye honoured at Sacred Crown Awards 2026
items.description: Prophet John Anokye, founder and leader of Worldwide Word Ministries, also known as The Hill City Church, has received the Prophetic Mentorship and Impact Award at the maiden Sacred Crown Awards 2026. The ceremony was held on Saturday, 31 October, at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel in Accra. The recognition honours Prophet Anokye for his contribution to prophetic ministry, spiritual leadership and mentorship. The awards initiative, held under the auspices of the Ga Mantse, His Royal Majesty King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, celebrates individuals and institutions making meaningful contributions to African heritage, spirituality, traditional leadership, healthcare, culture and community development. Prophet Anokye’s recognition highlights his years of service in Christian ministry and his work in equipping believers, developing emerging ministers and promoting spiritual growth. His journey in ministry dates back more than a decade. Speaking at the launch of his church’s 10th anniversary celebrations in February 2026, he disclosed that he received what he described as a divine instruction concerning his ministry in 2008, before formally establishing it. What began as a ministry with just 21 members has grown into Worldwide Word Ministries, The Hill City Church, with a wider vision of reaching people through the preaching and teaching of the Word of God. Beyond its regular church services, the ministry has established several programmes aimed at addressing different aspects of Christian life and personal development. These include the Healing in Health Conference, which has been running since 2015, the Prophetic Business Conference, the Finance Summit and the Prophetic Mentorship School. Through these initiatives, Prophet Anokye has sought to combine spiritual development with practical lessons in leadership, business, financial management and mentorship. A significant part of the ministry’s impact is reflected in its humanitarian interventions through I CARE Missions, the social outreach arm of Worldwide Word Ministries, which has been operating since the inception of the ministry. Through I CARE Missions, the church has supported orphans, provided scholarships to students, including beneficiaries outside the congregation, paid hospital bills, supported widows and extended assistance to the needy and vulnerable in society. The initiative also supports orphanages and hospitals as part of its broader commitment to improving lives and providing relief to individuals and families facing difficult circumstances. These interventions underscore the ministry’s commitment to extending its impact beyond the pulpit by combining spiritual leadership with practical acts of compassion, generosity and community service. Prophet Anokye’s ministry has also maintained a presence on television, connecting with viewers through Media General’s TV3 every Sunday morning at 7 am, where he shares messages centred on faith, biblical teachings and spiritual growth. The television platform has provided another avenue for the ministry to reach audiences beyond its church congregation, offering viewers an opportunity to engage with his teachings and ministry. The Sacred Crown recognition adds to the public acknowledgement of Prophet Anokye’s work in prophetic ministry, mentorship and humanitarian service. For Worldwide Word Ministries and its congregation, the honour represents an important milestone in a journey that continues to focus on spiritual development, raising believers and making a meaningful difference in people’s lives through service and community outreach. The Sacred Crown Awards brought together traditional authorities, religious leaders, policymakers, cultural figures and other personalities to celebrate contributions to Ghanaian and African society.

Un alunissage habité avant 2030 : la nouvelle approche chinoise pour décomposer les défis complexes de l’exploration lunaire
items.description: Wang Xiang, lors de la 7e Conférence académique du vol spatial habité de Chine, le 31 octobre） Le 31 octobre, lors de la 7e Conférence académique du vol spatial habité de Chine, Wang Xiang, directeur adjoint de la conception du programme chinois de vol spatial habité et concepteur en chef du programme d'exploration lunaire, a dévoilé un plan opérationnel détaillé‌ pour l'alunissage habité. Tout en réaffirmant l'objectif historique d'envoyer des astronautes chinois sur la Lune ‌d'ici la fin de‌ 2030, Wang Xiang a également révélé pour la première fois le déroulement complet et détaillé de la mission. La Chine adoptera une formule très caractéristique — « deux lancements, un alunissage » — qui, par une conception à la fois ingénieuse et pragmatique, permettra d'accomplir la mission habitée vers la Lune avec ‌des risques mieux maîtrisés et une efficacité renforcée, offrant une nouvelle voie de référence pour l'exploration spatiale profonde mondiale. Au début de la mission, une fusée Longue Marche 10 sera lancée la première et placera l'atterrisseur lunaire Lanyue sur la trajectoire de transfert vers la Lune. Parvenu dans la zone spatiale prévue, l'atterrisseur déploiera ses panneaux solaires, poursuivra de manière autonome sa route vers la Lune et se placera enfin en orbite circumlunaire, en attente de l'étape suivante. Une seconde fusée Longue Marche 10 s'envolera ensuite, emportant trois astronautes et le vaisseau habité Mengzhou. Après avoir parcouru les 380 000 kilomètres qui séparent la Terre de la Lune, le Mengzhou rejoindra avec précision l'orbite circumlunaire et réalisera un amarrage de haute précision avec l'atterrisseur Lanyue qui l'y attendra. L'amarrage une fois accompli, deux des trois astronautes entreront dans l'atterrisseur ; celui-ci se séparera alors du vaisseau habité et entamera une descente progressive vers la surface lunaire. Pendant la descente, le module de freinage, sa mission de décélération achevée, se détachera automatiquement : seul subsistera le module d'atterrissage, qui se posera en douceur dans la zone lunaire ‌ciblée‌. Les deux astronautes sortiront aussitôt pour mener une série de travaux scientifiques essentiels, notamment la marche sur le sol lunaire, les observations scientifiques et le prélèvement d'échantillons de sol lunaire. L'ensemble des travaux scientifiques accomplis sur la surface, l'atterrisseur Lanyue redécollera de manière autonome, regagnera l'orbite circumlunaire et réalisera un second amarrage avec le Mengzhou qui l'y attendra. Les deux astronautes rapporteront à bord du vaisseau habité les précieux échantillons de sol lunaire, complétant ainsi le transfert de l'équipage et du matériel. La passation terminée, les deux vaisseaux se sépareront et Mengzhou entamera son voyage de retour. À l'approche de la Terre, le module de service du vaisseau se détachera automatiquement ; la capsule de retour plongera dans l'atmosphère terrestre et, freinée progressivement par trois parachutes, raccompagnera en toute sécurité les trois astronautes au sol. Cette formule innovante de « deux lancements, un alunissage » a été largement saluée par les passionnés d'astronautique du monde entier, qui y voient une solution astronautique efficace, pragmatique et d'une grande ingéniosité. Comparé au schéma traditionnel, ce plan chinois présente plusieurs avantages marquants. D'abord, une sécurité accrue et des risques mieux maîtrisés : la mission une fois scindée, chaque segment de vol est plus simple, la marge de tolérance aux erreurs s'élargit considérablement et la probabilité d'un échec global s'en trouve réduite. Ensuite, une maturité technique et une aptitude au concret : amarrage en orbite, alunissage et décollage depuis la Lune, aller-retour en espace profond — toutes ces technologies clés ont été pleinement validées par les précédentes missions dans l’espace, et le système technique, stable et fiable, ne comporte aucune barrière inconnue. Enfin, un bon rapport coût-efficacité : le dispositif s'appuie sur les lanceurs et les vaisseaux existants, sans qu'il soit nécessaire d'engager des dépenses colossales pour développer un tout nouveau lanceur super lourd de très grande capacité, ce qui comprime fortement les cycles et les coûts de développement. (Chang'e-6) Ces deux dernières années, le programme chinois d'exploration lunaire a engrangé des résultats techniques de tout premier ordre, dont la mission Chang'e-6, menée à bien en 2024, offre la meilleure illustration : parvenue sur la face cachée de la Lune, une zone jusque-là très peu explorée par l'humanité, la sonde a réalisé, pour la première fois de l'histoire humaine, un retour d'échantillons prélevés sur la face cachée de la Lune par une mission inhabitée, rapportant un précieux sol lunaire extrait de l'ancien bassin Pôle Sud-Aitken. Cette avancée a comblé une lacune scientifique dans l'exploration de la face cachée de la Lune et accumule, pour les futures missions habitées, une expérience technique et des données scientifiques précieuses. La paix, l'ouverture et la coopération gagnant-gagnant constituent le consensus commun de l'exploration spatiale profonde, tout comme le principe de développement que l'astronautique chinoise n'a cessé de défendre. La Chine rejette résolument la mentalité figée de la course à l'espace et fait progresser l'exploration spatiale profonde à un rythme solide et graduel. Cette formule d'alunissage habité, à la fois peu risquée et très efficace, témoigne d'une maîtrise mûre et sûre des technologies d'exploration spatiale profonde ; elle offre un nouveau paradigme réalisable pour l'exploration lunaire humaine et aide l'humanité, main dans la main, à explorer l'immensité de l'univers et à repousser sans cesse les frontières de l'exploration spatiale profonde. Synthèse de Nadège YAMEOGO Source : CGTN Français

items.title: Big Chef Junior Season 5 finale set for November 8, GH₵20,000 at stake
items.description: Four young chefs will compete for the Big Chef Junior Season 5 title and a GH₵20,000 cash prize at the grand finale on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The stage is set for an exciting showdown as Joy Prime’s Big Chef Junior Season Five prepares to crown its ultimate winner at the Joy FM Car Park in Accra. After weeks of intense cooking challenges, emotional eliminations and impressive culinary displays, four young chefs, Afia, Akosua, Clara and Sethlyne, have secured their places in the grand finale, where they will compete for the coveted title and the cash prize. The event is scheduled to begin at 4:00 pm, with patrons encouraged to be seated by 2:00 pm. Adding to the excitement will be performances from popular Ghanaian comedian Funny Face, alongside talented young entertainers Maame Yaawells and Akorfa from DGL Academy, who are expected to bring an extra dose of excitement to the grand finale. Beyond the entertainment, all eyes will be on the four finalists as they face their biggest cooking challenge yet. For the final task, the contestants will be required to prepare one of four variations of fried rice: beef, chicken, pork or shrimp. The young chefs will select their dishes through a ballot on the day and must demonstrate the culinary skills, creativity and confidence they have developed throughout the competition, without assistance. The challenge will serve as the ultimate test of their growth after weeks of learning, competing and receiving guidance from judges Chef Michael and Chef Gigi. Season Five began with 12 young contestants, each determined to prove their abilities in the kitchen. From preparing traditional Ghanaian dishes such as ampesi, jollof rice and omo tuo to tackling creative cooking challenges, the contestants have experienced both victories and setbacks. The competition has also produced memorable moments, including multiple Star Chef wins, emotional farewells and remarkable improvements from contestants who initially struggled in the kitchen. Now, with just four contestants remaining, the race for the ultimate title is expected to be fiercely contested. Viewers also have a role to play in determining who emerges victorious. Supporters can vote for their favourite finalist by dialling 713 208# and following the prompts. Hosted by Michelle Agyekum, Big Chef Junior Season Five has continued to provide a platform for young culinary talents to showcase their creativity, build confidence and develop essential cooking skills. The grand finale will bring together contestants, their families, supporters and fans of the show to celebrate the young chefs’ achievements throughout the season. Big Chef Junior Season Five is supported by Gino, Frytol, Didi Shito, Sankofa Natural Spices, LEF Signature, Ginny, Fortune Spread, Wisdom Salt, Roch Electronics, Gari Mix, Reedy Vitamin C and CompuGhana. The grand finale comes off on Sunday, November 8, at the Joy FM Car Park in Accra, beginning at 4:00 pm. Four finalists, one ultimate winner and GH₵20,000 at stake. Who will be crowned the next Big Chef?

items.title: Big Ghun partners Betfox Ghana for 3,000 helmets distribution campaign
items.description: Award-winning filmmaker, rapper and creative personality Big Ghun has teamed up with BetfoxGhana to launch a nationwide road safety campaign to distribute more than 3,000 motorcycle helmets to riders across Ghana. The initiative comes at a time when motorcycle-related accidents continue to claim lives and leave families devastated. According to figures highlighted by Ghana’s Ministry of Transport, 1,345 of the 2,949 road fatalities recorded in 2025 involved motorcycle crashes, representing nearly 46 per cent of all road deaths that year. The situation remains worrying. Between January and September 2026 alone, Ghana recorded 2,151 road crash deaths and 12,230 injuries, according to the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service. For many Ghanaians, motorcycles are more than a means of transportation. They are a source of livelihood, a way to provide for loved ones and, sometimes, the only accessible means of getting around. The goal of the initiative is to help more riders return home safely to the people who depend on them. Campaign takes off in Ashaiman The first phase of the campaign officially commenced in Ashaiman, where Big Ghun and the Betfox Ghana team paid a courtesy visit to the Ashaiman District Police Commander, DSP Orlando Joseph Adzokpa. During the visit, the team donated a number of protective helmets to the police department as part of efforts to encourage safer motorcycle use and strengthen community road safety awareness. Following the engagement, the team moved into the streets of Ashaiman to distribute helmets directly to motorcycle riders. Beyond providing protective equipment, the initiative seeks to encourage responsible riding, greater awareness of road safety regulations and the consistent use of helmets by both riders and passengers. A mission beyond the numbers Although the campaign has set an initial target of distributing more than 3,000 helmets, the partners hope its impact will extend far beyond the number of helmets handed out. The initiative is built on the belief that protecting even one life can preserve an entire family’s future. A single road accident can change everything. It can take away a family’s provider, interrupt a young person’s dreams or leave loved ones dealing with losses that could have been prevented. Through this intervention, Betfox Ghana and Big Ghun hope to contribute to a culture where road safety becomes a shared responsibility rather than an afterthought. Taking the campaign across Ghana Following its commencement in Ashaiman, the team intends to extend the campaign to other communities within Greater Accra before expanding into additional regions across the country. Big Ghun has pledged to use his social media platforms to announce upcoming locations ahead of each visit, allowing motorcycle riders and community members to know when the campaign will reach their neighbourhoods. He has also expressed his willingness to work with the partners to extend the initiative beyond its initial distribution target should the need arise and additional resources become available. The long-term ambition is to inspire greater public consciousness about motorcycle safety and encourage other individuals, institutions and corporate bodies to contribute to protecting lives on Ghana’s roads. For the partners, the campaign is driven by the belief that at the end of every journey, someone is waiting for a loved one to come home. Sometimes, something as simple as wearing a quality helmet can make all the difference. One Helmet. One Life. One Safer Journey.

items.title: U17WWC: Tinubu urges Flamingos to stay focused ahead of the final
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their impressive victory over Brazil in Wednesday’s semi-final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The president described the team’s qualification for the final as a remarkable achievement that has brought immense pride and joy to millions of Nigerians at home and abroad. President Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, applauded the coaching crew and all those whose hard work and support contributed to the team’s successful campaign. As the Flamingos prepare to face Japan in the final, the President urges the players to remain focused, confident, and determined, assuring them of the prayers, goodwill, and unflinching support of the Nigerian nation. He said, “I encourage you to approach the final with the same fighting spirit and belief that have brought you this far. I have confidence in your ability to make history by winning the coveted world title. “I call on all Nigerians to rally behind the young ambassadors of the nation, whose achievements continue to showcase Nigeria’s sporting excellence and inspire a new generation of girls to pursue their dreams uninhibited. “Once again, Nigeria is proud of you. Go for the trophy, Flamingos!” he added. The post U17WWC: Tinubu urges Flamingos to stay focused ahead of the final appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bamako mérite mieux
items.description: © Internet À Bamako, se déplacer relève encore trop souvent de l’improvisation. Sotrama, taxis jaunes, moto-taxis et véhicules particuliers assurent l’essentiel d’un service qui devrait pourtant relever d’une véritable politique publique de mobilité. Chacun comble un vide, mais l’ensemble produit embouteillages, arrêts anarchiques, concurrence désordonnée et insécurité pour les usagers. Une capitale de plusieurs millions d’habitants ne peut durablement fonctionner ainsi. À Dakar, comme dans d’autres grandes villes africaines, l’État et les collectivités ont développé des réseaux publics de bus et, plus récemment, des systèmes de transport de masse. Bamako n’est pas condamnée à attendre un tramway pour commencer à s’organiser. L’idée n’est d’ailleurs pas nouvelle. En mars 2018, lors de sa visite au Mali, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan avait proposé un projet de Métrobus pour moderniser la circulation dans la capitale. Il n’a pas vu le jour. Plus récemment, le Mali a signé avec le constructeur russe KAMAZ un contrat portant sur 350 véhicules, pour plus de 30 milliards de francs CFA. La flotte annoncée comprend notamment des bus urbains, avec en perspective maintenance, formation et assemblage local. Ces investissements devraient être l’occasion de penser enfin un réseau cohérent : lignes identifiées, horaires, arrêts aménagés, tarifs connus, correspondances et desserte périurbaine. Les transporteurs privés peuvent y avoir leur place, mais dans un cadre organisé. Bamako aspire à devenir une capitale moderne. Cela passe aussi par la manière dont ses habitants vont travailler, étudier, se soigner ou simplement rentrer chez eux. Le transport urbain n’est pas un service secondaire. C’est une infrastructure essentielle de la ville et de son avenir collectif. Massiré Diop

items.title: Ghana targets financial health with new inclusion strategy for 2027–2031
items.description: Ghana is taking steps to shift its financial inclusion agenda from expanding access to financial services to improving the financial health and well-being of citizens. The Ministry of Finance, in collaboration with the United Nations Secretary-General’s Special Advocate for Inclusive Finance for Development, Her Majesty Queen Máxima of the Netherlands, has inaugurated a National Technical Working Committee to spearhead the development of the country’s second National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy (2027–2031). The strategy, which is being developed under the theme “ Shaping Ghana’s Next Frontier in Financial Inclusion and Development,” is expected to provide a roadmap for improving access to financial services, strengthening financial resilience and promoting economic empowerment. Speaking at the inauguration, Deputy Minister of Finance, Hon. Thomas Ampem Nyarko, said government is committed to ensuring that financial inclusion translates into tangible improvements in the lives of Ghanaians. He noted that although the country has made significant progress in expanding access to financial services, more needed to be done to ensure citizens could use these services to improve their financial security. According to him, data from the World Bank’s Global Findex 2025 shows that more than eight in every ten Ghanaian adults now own a financial account. However, the 2021 Financial Inclusion and Demand-Side Survey found that only 22 percent of adults were financially healthy. “We have become good at opening accounts. We must now become better at making accounts improve lives,” he said. Mr Nyarko explained that financial inclusion must go beyond owning bank or mobile money accounts to providing people with the financial tools to withstand economic shocks, build assets and plan for the future. He said the new strategy would prioritise responsible financial services, digital innovation, consumer protection, financial literacy and resilience, particularly among women, young people, farmers, informal sector workers and small businesses. The Deputy Minister also announced plans to establish a Financial Inclusion Council to strengthen coordination and accountability among stakeholders, alongside a financial health framework to measure the financial well-being of households. He said government is working towards launching the new strategy in the first half of 2027. Her Majesty Queen Máxima has emphasised the need for Ghana to shift its focus from financial inclusion alone to achieving measurable improvements in the financial health of its citizens. She described financial inclusion as a means to an end, arguing that access to financial accounts does not automatically translate into improved living conditions. “Financial inclusion is a means to an end, not an end in itself. You don’t become better by having an account. You’re going to become better when you have an insurance that is going to protect you when there’s drought,” she said. Queen Máxima identified four key components of financial health: managing day-to-day finances, building resilience against financial shocks, pursuing financial goals and maintaining confidence in one’s financial future. She explained that households must be equipped with the tools to manage income and expenditure, save towards anticipated expenses and protect themselves against unexpected events such as illness, accidents, droughts and fires. She also stressed the importance of emergency savings, affordable insurance and accessible pension schemes, particularly for workers in the informal sector. Queen Máxima noted that Ghana had made considerable progress in financial inclusion, with access to financial services increasing from about 30 percent in 2011 to approximately 80 percent currently. She said the country was at a critical point to ensure that the progress made in expanding financial access translates into improved financial well-being. The Queen further called for the adoption of a broader financial health measurement framework that captures the experiences of different groups, including women, older persons and rural and urban dwellers. She urged financial institutions to assess the financial health of their customers and develop innovative products that respond to their needs. She cited the example of savings products that automatically set aside a portion of customers’ income to encourage regular savings. Queen Máxima also called for stronger collaboration among financial sector regulators to expand access to affordable insurance and pension products, while promoting digital payments and data sharing to improve financial services. She stressed that achieving financial health would require coordinated efforts from government, financial institutions, regulators and development partners. “My partners and I are going to be accompanying you along the way in order to develop this financial health and make it a reality,” she assured. The inauguration brings together financial sector regulators, financial institutions, development partners and other stakeholders to guide the development of Ghana’s second National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy.

items.title: Transporteurs : une aide de 60% et jusqu’à 5.600 dhs pour préserver le pouvoir d’achat
items.description: À l’issue du Conseil de gouvernement de ce jeudi 5 novembre, le ministre du transport et de la logistique, Abdessamad Kayouh, a détaillé les modalités de la reprise du soutien accordé aux professionnels du transport. Ce dispositif, renouvelé tous les quinze jours, vise à atténuer les répercussions de la hausse des coûts du transport sur les prix des produits de première nécessité et sur les déplacements des citoyens. © Mounir Mehimdate La reprise de cette aide intervient dans un contexte marqué par les fluctuations des cours du pétrole et les incertitudes pesant sur les approvisionnements. « Depuis cette période, nous avons constaté que l’incertitude s’est installée et qu’elle persiste », a déclaré Abdessamad Kayouh, en référence à la crise sanitaire du Covid-19 et à la guerre en Ukraine. Le ministre a rappelé que la hausse des prix du pétrole, notamment du gasoil, avait particulièrement affecté le Maroc après la sortie de la crise sanitaire, à partir du 26 mars 2022. « Le Maroc, comme tous les autres pays, vit avec cette incertitude et fait face à ces fluctuations », a-t-il souligné, en relevant que si les prix du pétrole avaient baissé jeudi, leur évolution future demeurait imprévisible. © Mounir Mehimdate « L’essentiel, c’est que le gouvernement assume ses responsabilités », a-t-il insisté, en présentant le soutien aux transporteurs comme un moyen de préserver la continuité de l’approvisionnement en marchandises et de limiter les répercussions des coûts logistiques sur les consommateurs. Un soutien couvrant 60 % des différentes tranches Le ministre a affirmé que le gouvernement avait renforcé son intervention pour accompagner les professionnels du secteur. « Ce soutien représente 60 %, toutes les tranches confondues. C’est la première fois que nous atteignons un niveau de 60 % par rapport à la première aide accordée », a-t-il déclaré. L’objectif, a-t-il expliqué, est de garantir l’approvisionnement en l’ensemble des produits destinés à la consommation des citoyens « à des prix raisonnables ». © Mounir Mehimdate Kayouh a rappelé que le transport constituait une composante importante du prix final des marchandises. Pour illustrer cet impact, il a évoqué le cas d’un produit acheminé d’Agadir à Nador, qui doit nécessairement supporter des frais de transport. « Si le transport coûte 4 dirhams, alors qu’il coûtait auparavant 30 centimes, il n’est pas raisonnable que cette hausse ait un impact aussi important », a-t-il estimé, soulignant la nécessité d’intervenir pour limiter la répercussion de ces coûts sur les prix à la consommation. Le ministre a indiqué que les montants de l’aide avaient été définis pour une période de quinze jours, allant du 1er au 15 novembre. Il a précisé qu’il ne souhaitait pas entrer dans les détails des calculs, mais présenter les montants attribués à chaque catégorie de transporteurs. © Mounir Mehimdate Les montants accordés aux différentes catégories de transport Selon le ministre Kayouh, les autocars de transport interurbain de voyageurs bénéficieront d’une aide de 5.600 dirhams pour cette période de quinze jours. Le dispositif vise notamment à éviter que les coûts supplémentaires ne se répercutent sur les tarifs payés par les passagers, a-t-il précisé. Pour le transport de marchandises, les montants varient selon la capacité des véhicules, comprise entre 3,5 et 25 tonnes. Les véhicules d’une charge de 3,5 tonnes recevront 2.080 dirhams, ceux de 14 tonnes 2.720 dirhams, tandis que les véhicules de 19 tonnes bénéficieront de 3.360 dirhams pour quinze jours. Les tracteurs routiers, utilisés pour tracter les semi-remorques, percevront pour leur part 4.800 dirhams. Les petits taxis bénéficieront d’une aide de 1.280 dirhams, contre 1.760 dirhams pour les grands taxis. Les autobus de transport public urbain recevront 4.960 dirhams pour la période concernée. Dans le monde rural, les véhicules de transport mixte bénéficieront d’un soutien de 1.440 dirhams. Le transport touristique, toutes catégories confondues, est également concerné. Le ministre a évoqué des montants allant de 800 à 2.240 dirhams, tout en mentionnant une aide de 1.220 dirhams pour la deuxième catégorie. Les véhicules de remorquage et de dépannage ont également été intégrés au dispositif, avec une aide de 800 dirhams. Enfin, les véhicules assurant le transport de personnel pour le compte de tiers bénéficieront de 960 dirhams pour la première catégorie et de 800 dirhams pour la deuxième. Une aide renouvelée tous les quinze jours Abdessamad Kayouh a insisté sur le fait que cet effort gouvernemental ne constituait pas une initiative ponctuelle. Il s’inscrit, selon lui, dans une démarche visant à faire face aux conséquences économiques et psychologiques de la hausse des prix. « Nous sommes face à une réalité, à un effet psychologique lié notamment au fait de voir le prix du gasoil atteindre 17 dirhams », a-t-il déclaré, évoquant les guerres et les perturbations de l’approvisionnement parmi les facteurs expliquant cette situation. Le ministre a également annoncé que le gouvernement prendrait en charge la facture de l’aide correspondant à la période allant du 15 octobre au 1er novembre, avant de poursuivre le versement du soutien selon une périodicité de quinze jours. Cette régularité doit permettre de maintenir l’accompagnement des professionnels du transport dans un contexte de volatilité des prix. L’objectif final, a rappelé Abdessamad Kayouh, demeure la préservation du pouvoir d’achat, tant pour les citoyens qui utilisent les moyens de transport que pour les consommateurs qui subissent les répercussions des coûts logistiques sur les prix des marchandises. « L’objectif est de préserver le pouvoir d’achat, aussi bien des citoyens qui se déplacent que des consommateurs, en limitant l’impact de ces coûts sur le prix final des marchandises qui leur sont destinées », a-t-il conclu. The post Transporteurs : une aide de 60% et jusqu’à 5.600 dhs pour préserver le pouvoir d’achat appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 2027: Ajimobi, Folarin, Adelabu lead Oyo APC reconciliation push
items.description: By Adeola Badru Efforts to resolve internal divisions and strengthen the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 general elections have gained momentum following a meeting involving prominent party leaders. The meeting, led by former Oyo State First Lady and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Austria, Mrs Florence Ajimobi, brought together the Oyo State Coordinator of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Teslim Kolawole Folarin; Senator Abdulfatai Buhari, representing Oyo North Senatorial District; former Minister of Power, Chief Adebayo Adelabu; and Barrister Akeem Agbaje. The meeting focused on resolving internal disagreements, promoting inclusive leadership and rebuilding unity within the party ahead of the 2027 elections. According to sources familiar with the discussions, participants emphasised the need to set aside personal differences and competing interests in the collective interest of the party. They reportedly agreed that greater cohesion among party leaders and stakeholders would strengthen the APC’s political structure and improve its chances in the state. The discussions also highlighted the importance of sustained consultations among critical stakeholders and ensuring that different tendencies within the party were accommodated in its decision-making process. A major issue raised at the meeting was the need to translate calls for reconciliation into concrete actions aimed at rebuilding trust, addressing grievances and encouraging cooperation among party leaders and members. With the 2027 elections approaching, the engagement was seen as part of renewed efforts by influential party figures to harmonise interests and prevent lingering disagreements from affecting the APC’s preparations. The participants also underscored the importance of developing a collective political strategy capable of carrying all stakeholders along and strengthening the party’s electoral prospects across Oyo State. items.title: The Inconvenient Truth: When parties take turns winning while the nation keeps losing
items.description: When political rivalry grows so fierce that a country’s progress is treated as an electoral threat, democracy becomes a relay race in which the baton is passed faithfully from party to party while the nation itself never leaves the starting line. The bill, as always, is sent to ordinary citizens and to generations not yet born. By Ing. Prof. Douglas Boateng, Chartered Director UK | Chartered Engineer UK | Fellow, Institute of Directors UK | Fellow, Ghana Institution of Engineering | Governance, Industrialisation and Supply Chain Strategist | Founder, Boardroom Governance Summit | Founder and Scriber, NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) Cheering For Turbulence At Thirty Thousand Feet Imagine two political parties aboard the same aircraft, one seated in the cockpit and the other in the cabin, waiting with visible impatience for its turn at the controls. The pilots make mistakes, some of their decisions deserve robust criticism, and the passengers have every right to demand better navigation and a safer journey. Then something extraordinary happens, because instead of insisting that the crew correct course, a few passengers begin quietly hoping for enough turbulence to discredit whoever is flying, and some look disappointed whenever the ride becomes smooth. The pilots, for their part, grow so busy proving their critics wrong that they ignore perfectly sensible warnings about the state of the engines. Now imagine that the aircraft is a nation, with government in the cockpit, the opposition in the cabin, citizens in economy class and the economy itself holding everyone aloft, and the absurdity suddenly becomes painfully familiar. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) observes that “only a confused passenger celebrates the pilot’s failure while forgetting that both are travelling in the same aircraft.” The Economy Does Not Carry A Party Card We create political parties to offer competing visions of national progress, and we hold elections so that leaders remain answerable, yet competition can quietly decay into something closer to hostility. A factory closes and families see unemployment while strategists see campaign material, a currency weakens and businesses see rising costs while rivals see an opportunity for embarrassment, and a stalled hospital project becomes less a tragedy for the sick than a debate about whose fault it is. Scrutiny of setbacks is essential, but there is a profound moral difference between exposing failure so that it can be corrected and privately welcoming failure because it might be useful at the ballot box. Inflation never checks a membership card before raising the price of bread, and unemployment has never once asked a young graduate how she voted. Perhaps each party should run its own electricity grid, hospitals and currency for its loyal supporters, so that everyone could enjoy only the consequences of their preferred party’s decisions. Sadly, economics has never shown the slightest interest in party colours, and it is unlikely to start now. The Political Tailor And The Recycled Idea Opposition is indispensable to democracy, for it exposes wrongdoing, challenges weak policy and presents alternatives. The difficulty is not disagreement but the strange alchemy by which disagreement becomes an incentive to see the nation stumble. A promising reform may be resisted because its success would flatter the governing party, while a government may reject a sensible opposition proposal simply because accepting it would look like defeat. Thus unfolds a curious national theatre in which one party proposes an idea, the other condemns it, an election is held, the condemning party wins, and the very same idea reappears a year later dressed in a political uniform. The policy has not changed; only the tailor has. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) captures the comedy and the cost together: “when a good idea becomes bad because an opponent proposed it, national progress becomes a prisoner of political ownership.” The Most Expensive Habit Of All Is Starting Again The deepest economic wound inflicted by excessive polarisation is the death of continuity, because industrialisation demands patience, infrastructure demands persistence and education reform demands consistency, while electoral cycles are comparatively short. When an incoming government judges an inherited project chiefly by its political parentage rather than its economic merit, the nation pays twice, first to begin the project and again to abandon it. Nigeria’s Presidential Projects Assessment Committee reported in 2011 that 11,886 federal government projects lay uncompleted or abandoned, requiring an estimated 7.78 trillion naira to finish, and the Ajaokuta steel complex has stood for decades as a monument to billions spent without sustained production. A bridge does not become structurally unsound because a rival laid its foundation, and a hospital does not become unnecessary because the ribbon was cut by the previous administration. As NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) warns, “a nation that demolishes yesterday’s foundations whenever leadership changes should not be surprised when tomorrow’s buildings remain unfinished.” What Singapore, Seoul And Gaborone Understood Investors fully expect political parties to disagree; what they need is the reassurance that contracts will be honoured, regulations applied consistently and institutions kept professionally competent whoever wins. Singapore’s transformation rested on long range planning and institutional steadiness, South Korea’s industrial rise required decades of coordinated investment in skills and technology, and Botswana’s careful stewardship of its diamond wealth shows what institutional stability can achieve. These countries followed very different paths, and none offers a template for Africa to copy, yet they share one lesson that deserves to be framed and hung in every parliament: long term development cannot be left entirely at the mercy of individual political fortunes. Extra Time In A Match That Nobody Wins Polarisation also has the curious effect of turning every national challenge into a football. Unemployment is kicked from one end of the pitch to the other, healthcare is headed into the stands, public debt is dribbled endlessly in midfield, commentators deliver passionate analysis, supporters roar, and social media erupts, yet the problem remains exactly where it started. The only real difference between our politics and a football tournament is that football matches eventually end, whereas our political arguments appear to enjoy unlimited extra time with no penalty shootout in sight. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) offers a sobering verdict: “when leaders spend more time scoring political points than solving national problems, citizens become spectators in a match where everybody loses.” A Young Continent Cannot Wait For A Ceasefire The heaviest price of permanent political warfare falls on those with the least say in starting it. With a median age of roughly 19, Africa is home to the youngest population on earth, and that demographic promise could become an engine of prosperity or a source of profound frustration depending on whether productive investment, industrialisation and skills development are sustained across successive governments. A graduate seeking work gains nothing from rival histories of who created unemployment, an entrepreneur battling unreliable power needs electricity rather than explanations. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) reminds us that “young people cannot build their futures from political promises that are demolished before they become economic opportunities.” A society that keeps postponing reform for the sake of rivalry may one day discover that its young people have lost patience not with one party, but with the entire political establishment. Patriotism Must Be Larger Than Party Colours Political parties are vital instruments of representation, but a party is not the nation, its leaders are temporary custodians of public authority, and its supporters were citizens long before they collected their membership cards. Yet polarisation tempts some citizens to celebrate national achievements selectively, depending on which party receives the credit, and makes others reluctant to acknowledge genuine progress because doing so would require a compliment to the other side. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) sets a demanding standard: “true patriotism is revealed when you can celebrate your country’s progress even when your preferred party receives none of the applause.” From Political Warfare To National Purpose The answer is not permanent consensus, for democracy depends on disagreement and on the freedom to change governments, but on distinguishing healthy competition from the national priorities that deserve continuity. Countries should strengthen independent national planning institutions with long term mandates, and parties should agree a small charter of strategic priorities, such as foundational education, public health, water security, critical infrastructure and institutional integrity, while continuing to argue vigorously about how best to achieve them. Inherited projects should face independent technical and financial assessment before anyone decides to continue, restructure or end them, with the central question being value for money and value for development rather than political parentage. Parliamentary oversight should become more constructive without becoming less rigorous, public institutions should be staffed and judged on competence rather than loyalty, and citizens and the media should ask whether a policy works before asking who proposed it. Finally, every party must cultivate the maturity to applaud national achievements delivered under its rivals, because, as NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) puts it, “a party may win an election by proving its opponent failed, but a nation only wins when its people succeed.” The Unborn Child Holds No Membership Card Picture an African child born twenty five years from now, who will inherit the schools we build or neglect, the hospitals we equip or abandon, the industries we develop or forgo and the debts we accumulate, but none of our campaign slogans. One day that child may study our debates and ask, “if you knew that development required continuity and cooperation, why did you spend so long proving that the other party could do nothing worthwhile?” We might mumble that an election was approaching, and history may listen politely, but the child will still be living with the consequences. Let us therefore return to our aircraft, where pilots may change and crews may propose different routes, but the engines must be maintained, the navigation must work, and nobody should ever cheer turbulence merely because it might embarrass whoever occupies the cockpit. We must learn to disagree without destroying, to compete without sabotaging and to transfer power without repeatedly transferring the country back to the starting line. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) leaves us with a final reflection: “when political parties wait for one another to fail, a nation may spend generations waiting for itself to succeed.” Political victory may belong to one party, but economic failure belongs to every citizen, and the Africa we desire remains, as it always has been, in our own hands. About the Author Ing. Professor Douglas K. Boateng is a strategist in governance, industrialisation and supply chains, and serves as a professional chairperson, an international Chartered Director (UK) and a Chartered Engineer (UK). A Pan-Africanist and social entrepreneur at heart, he has spent his career working across public institutions, corporate boards and industrial policy, in Africa and beyond, guided by the conviction that strong institutions are built one honest decision at a time. His contributions to industry and academia have earned him more than six lifetime achievement awards. He is the founder of NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom), a collection of daily aphorisms he has written and shared since late 2019, distilling decades of experience advising governments, boards, and enterprises on governance, accountability, and institutional resilience into words meant to challenge and endure. He convenes the Boardroom Governance Summit, Africa’s largest boardroom-focused summit, and writes a widely read weekly op-ed series titled “Inconvenient Truth” and “What Is Wrong With Us”, featured on some of the region’s leading digital media platforms. Professor Boateng can be reached via LinkedIn or at info@panavest.com . © 2026 Ing. Prof. Douglas Boateng. All rights reserved.

items.title: Ablakwa should allow ministry departments to function – Kwesi Pratt
items.description: Managing Editor of The Insight newspaper, Kwesi Pratt Jnr, has advised Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to allow officials within the ministry to handle administrative matters instead of personally taking the lead in addressing every issue. Mr Pratt said the minister’s approach to public communication and the handling of ministry-related matters could expose him to unnecessary scrutiny and potential criticism arising from administrative decisions. The veteran journalist said the Foreign Affairs Minister occupies a high-level government position that requires careful attention to the responsibilities and risks associated with the office. “I have a little advice for the minister himself. It’s a huge position and comes with huge responsibility… And anybody occupying that position ought to take steps, take steps to distance himself from the potential fallout of some administrative actions,” he said. Mr Pratt argued that the ministry has an established administrative structure comprising deputy ministers, chief directors and departmental heads, who should be allowed to perform their respective functions. He said the minister should intervene only when issues cannot be resolved through the appropriate administrative channels. “That is why in the ministry, you have a minister, you have Deputies, you have Chief Directors, you have Directors for different desks. There are so many departments in that ministry. The ministers should allow the departments to function and the officers to function. “The minister is the last resort. When everything has gone haywire, when nothing has been solved, that’s when the minister starts to think,” he said. Mr Pratt also questioned why the minister appeared to be the main spokesperson on issues concerning the ministry, arguing that its public relations department and other responsible officials should ordinarily handle routine administrative communication. “Ministers are public relations officers. And yet, it is always the minister who is standing there, ready to face the storm. What is your public relations department supposed to do?” he asked. He said the practice of ministers personally taking responsibility for public communication could expose them to criticism over matters that should ordinarily be handled by departments and agencies. Mr Pratt further called for proper training and orientation for ministers after their appointments, arguing that political loyalty and campaign contributions should not be the only considerations in preparing individuals for public office. “Just throwing them into the crowd doesn’t help the ministers. It doesn’t help the government. It doesn’t help the country. It doesn’t help anybody,” he said. He spoke on Metro TV. Mr Pratt’s comments come amid pressure on Mr Ablakwa from the New Patriotic Party (NPP), whose Youth Wing has called on President John Dramani Mahama to remove him from office over alleged financial irregularities in the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. The party has questioned the reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians, demanding an independent audit and the publication of supporting invoices and payment records. It has also called for investigations into allegations surrounding the sale of diplomatic and service passports. The NPP’s National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fuseini Yakubu, led a demonstration in Accra on November 3, 2026, during which protesters presented a petition containing the party’s demands to the Presidency. The allegations and demands have not, in themselves, established any wrongdoing by the minister.

items.title: New economy to ensure a stronger economy delivers financial security for Ghanaians
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has said Ghana’s economic progress must translate into greater financial security for its people, describing household wellbeing as a key goal of the New Economy. The Minister made the remarks after hosting Her Majesty Queen Máxima of the Netherlands, whom he congratulated on her Financial Health campaign. “A stronger economy must mean greater financial security for our people,” Dr Forson said. His remarks linked the pursuit of a stronger economy to the everyday financial concerns of Ghanaians, including their ability to manage their money, provide security for their families and plan for the future. Reflecting on the visit, the Minister said he was honoured to welcome the Queen and acknowledged her efforts to promote financial health. “Earlier today, I had the honour of hosting Her Majesty Queen Máxima of the Netherlands. I congratulated her on her Financial Health campaign,” he said. Dr Forson highlighted three connected ambitions for the New Economy. They are greater control over personal finances, stronger family security and increased confidence in the country’s future. “Through the New Economy, we aim to give more Ghanaians greater control over their finances, greater security for their families and greater confidence in the future we are building together,” he stated.

items.title: Three Ghanaian authors to represent country at Sharjah International Book Fair
items.description: Three Ghanaian authors, Oswald Okaitei, Elizabeth-Irene Baitie and Ruby Goka, will represent Ghana at the 2026 Sharjah International Book Fair in the United Arab Emirates. The Consulate of Ghana in Dubai and the Northern Emirates, with sponsorship from BOST Energies, is leading the country’s participation in the fair, which runs from 4 to 15 November 2026. The participation marks Ghana’s first official appearance at the fair and is a step towards attracting investment, creating opportunities and building networks for the Ghanaian book industry. It also provides a platform to showcase the works of Ghanaian creative writers and connect local authors with the international literary community attending the fair in Sharjah. Selected for the initiative are three Ghanaian authors who have established themselves in the literary field: Ruby Goka, Elizabeth-Irene Baitie and Oswald Okaitei. The trio, who previously represented Ghana at Storymoja, one of Africa’s biggest and most prestigious literary festivals in Kenya, are expected to exhibit their works alongside those of other Ghanaian authors, participate in sessions at the fair and host a special Ghana Book Reading session at a selected venue in Sharjah. Elizabeth-Irene Baitie is a multiple award-winning Ghanaian author of eight published novels for children and young adults. Her work has been published in Ghana, Nigeria, the USA, the UK, Italy and Brazil, with a Japanese edition forthcoming. Her stories bring Ghana vividly to life for a global readership. Her first children’s book, A Saint in Brown Sandals , won the Macmillan Writer’s Prize for Africa. She won first prize in the Burt Award for African Literature for both The Twelfth Heart and The Dorm Challenge , with further Burt Award recognition for Rattling in the Closet and The Lion’s Whisper . Her middle-grade novels Crossing the Stream and Flying Up the Mountain both earned starred reviews from Kirkus Reviews and received Children’s Africana Book Award honours in 2022 and 2024, respectively. Oswald Okaitei is a Ghanaian poet, spoken-word artiste, playwright, storyteller and literary activist. His creative journey began in childhood, when he featured on Ghana’s popular children’s storytelling programme, By the Fireside . He is known for his thought-provoking poetry, dramatic performances and works that explore African identity, Pan-Africanism, history, social justice and cultural heritage. His literary works include A Wreath to Awoonor , In the Bag of a Woman and Mandela: The Soul of His Earth . Okaitei has represented Ghana at international literary festivals and continues to champion reading culture, literary development and the promotion of Ghanaian literature. Through his creative expression and advocacy, he uses literature as an instrument for cultural preservation, social transformation and national consciousness. The Ghana Book booth at the fair is located at Pavilion 6, Booths 023-024. It will exhibit literary works from Ghana and by Ghanaian authors and publishers.

items.title: Davido, Kwesi Arthur, Kweku Smoke, Lasmid, others billed for 2026 Tidal Rave Festival
items.description: It’s another year and Tidal Rave Festival is taking over the shores of Accra with hitmakers Davido, Kwesi Arthur, Kweku Smoke, Lasmid and other amazing artistes, MCs and DJs. Next Saturday, Africa’s biggest beach festival, Tidal Rave Festival, is getting ready to welcome Ravers to the beach for another exciting experience on 14th November, 2026. The festival, which will be held at La Palm Royal Beach Hotel, is being curated with the theme “No Raver Left Behind”, with tickets available at www.tidalravefestival.com . “Every friend group has its characters. The one who starts the plans, the one who gets everyone on board, the one who handles the food, and the one who makes sure nobody misses out. Different personalities, different interests, but somehow, they always find their way into the same plan. And when the memories are made, everyone has a story to tell,” Awo Somuah-Ampadu, Regional Lead of Echo Live at EchoHouse , said. That is the beauty of experiencing things together. The music, the laughter, the unexpected moments and the stories that follow become part of a shared history. It is often the people standing beside us who make an experience worth remembering. The theme puts friendship and togetherness at the heart of the festival, celebrating the people who make the experience what it is. From the music and fashion to creativity and the shared moments in between, Tidal Rave is inviting Ravers to bring their people along and make this year’s edition one to remember together. “Tidal Rave has always been about bringing young people together through experiences that stay with them. With #NoRaverLeftBehind, we want to put the friendships behind those experiences in the spotlight. We want Ravers to look forward to the festival not only because of what they will see or do, but because of who they will share it with. That sense of togetherness is central to what we are creating this year,” said Beryl Agyekum Ayaaba, CEO of EchoHouse , curators of Tidal Rave Festival. Bringing the Squad Into the Experience From group activities and shared spaces to opportunities to capture moments with friends, the intention is to make the experience feel personal to every Raver while bringing different groups together under one shared identity. The brands joining Tidal Rave are part of that wider experience, each bringing a different presence to the festival. Johnnie Walker returns with its own dedicated brand experience, adding another dimension to the Tidal Rave journey for Ravers to discover and enjoy with their squads. Blue Jeans joins the squad this year, bringing the energy that keeps Ravers moving, from the first beat to the final dance. Coca-Cola returns as a familiar part of the Tidal Rave experience, while Nescafé and *959# joins the mix, adding to the collection of brand partners coming together for this year’s festival. Across the experience, these partnerships form part of the wider environment in which Ravers can connect, discover and enjoy the day with their people. Other brand partners include Pepsodent, and Munchee. “We want to think about Tidal Rave from the perspective of the Ravers coming with their friends. How do they spend the day together? What can they discover, take part in and remember afterwards? Those questions are informing how we approach the festival experience this year. #NoRaverLeftBehind means creating more opportunities for people to feel included, participate together and make the day their own,” Awo Somuah-Ampadu added. With #NoRaverLeftBehind, Tidal Rave 2026 is inviting every Raver to think beyond making individual plans and urging them to start bringing their people into the picture. Whether it is the squad that has attended together for years or the group experiencing Tidal Rave for the first time, the idea remains the same: the experience is better when everyone gets to be part of it. On November 14, La Palm Royal Beach Hotel will welcome Ravers for another edition of Tidal Rave, with friendship, shared experiences and a sense of belonging at the heart of the festival.

items.title: Why did the ECP postpone local govt polls in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday decided to hold the first phase of local government elections in Punjab on Feb 7, 2027, but postponed them in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa until further orders. According to the electoral watchdog, it halted all preparations for local government elections until further orders after the federal government extended the suspension of Article 140-A of the Constitution — which requires the provinces to establish elected local governments, and decentralise political, administrative and financial powers to them — to the entire province a day earlier. The decision came even though the ECP ordered on Oct 28 that polls be held immediately in those districts where delimitation had been completed, excluding those included in the 12 districts with special emergency measures. Federal cabinet extends suspension of Article 140-A On Wednesday, the federal cabinet transferred the powers of the KP chi­ef minister, who became non-functional after the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency on Oct 11, to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. According to an official handout from the government, the move was meant to ensure the smooth execution of administrative affairs, improve governance and handle day-to-day matters during the provincial state of emergency. On Thursday, it emerged that the government also extended the suspension of Article 140-A to the entire province. The decision was notified through an order issued by the Cabinet Division and published in the Gazette of Pakistan on Nov 4. The order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, referred to the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11. It also noted that the governor had already been directed to assume control of the provincial government. Under the new order, Article 140-A will no longer apply to the remainder of the province, in addition to the designated districts where it already stood suspended. “The governor will now also exercise the powers of the KP chief minister under the Constitution, the laws and rules in force in the province and the KP government Rules of Business, 1985,” the order stated. It added that the governor will keep the federal government informed of all executive actions taken under the proclamation through monthly reports. Subsequently, the ECP on Thursday decided to halt preparations for local government polls in KP. What does this mean? Explaining the decision, a senior ECP official told Dawn that Article 140-A is the provision that makes local governments mandatory in Pakistan. He said it obliges each province to establish a local government system by law and devolve political, administrative and financial authority to elected local representatives and also makes holding local government elections the ECP’s constitutional responsibility. The official said the provision was inserted through the 18th Amendment in 2010 to ensure that local governments were a constitutional requirement, not a favour granted by a chief minister. He said that once Article 140-A is made inapplicable, the legal basis for holding local government elections disappears, along with the obligation to maintain an elected local government system and to devolve power and funds to it. In such a situation, he added, executive authority is concentrated in the governor, without elected local bodies as a counterweight. The official said the suspension was framed as a consequence of the emergency and would remain in force until it is withdrawn or the emergency ends, or it is struck down by a court.
