items.title: ‘Justice well served’, Keyamo lauds court ruling against Atiku, ADC
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, SAN, has welcomed Thursday’s Federal High Court judgment that sacked the Senator David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress ADC, declaring that “justice may be slow, but it is always sure!” In the judgment delivered on Thursday, Justice Peter Lifu declared the Mark-led Caretaker Committee as illegal and invalidated all actions taken on its behalf. These included the nomination of a former vice president, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the ADC’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general election. Reacting to the outcome, Keyamo said the manner in which the party was taken over could not stand. “You cannot invade a political party owned and built by Nigerians and hijack it with the connivance of a so-called National Chairman without a prior meeting and approval of a mini National Convention or the National Executive Committee,” he said. The minister added that those behind the takeover could not “bluff your way out of such a brazen act by blaming and blackmailing the ruling Party for a misfortune deliberately stocked by you.” The judgment followed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, filed by the party’s former National Deputy Chairman (North-East), Nafiu Bala Gombe. He asked the court to nullify all actions taken by the Mark-led leadership, arguing that following the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he was qualified to take over the leadership of the party. The defendants were the ADC, the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Senator Mark, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola and Chief Nwosu. Gombe also asked the court to stop Senator Mark and Aregbesola from presenting themselves as National Chairman and National Secretary, respectively, insisting that their emergence violated the party’s constitution and the Electoral Act. Justice Lifu upheld the plaintiff’s claims and granted his reliefs. Keyamo insisted that the court acted on the law and not on public feeling. “Sorry, but the law is decided on facts and evidence, rather than sentiments and outrage by a group of people,” he said. The ruling came barely 24 hours after Atiku held a rally in Sokoto State as part of his campaign for the January 16, 2027 presidential election. INEC had earlier published his name as a presidential candidate, and he has since picked a former Governor of Rivers State, Mr Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate. The ADC has said it will challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The party’s National Welfare Secretary, Mr Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was joined in the suit as an interested party, announced the decision to appeal. Keyamo, however, dismissed the notion that the judgment endangers democracy. “It is not only when a certain Atiku Abubakar contests the presidency that democracy is not in danger. The ADC as a party is well and alive and populated by people and original leaders who are no less Nigerians than David Mark and his illegal band of marauders,” he added. items.title: Una nueva oleada de falsas amenazas de bomba afecta al menos a 20 aviones con destino a ciudades europeas
items.description: El tráfico aéreo en toda Europa se ha visto afectado este jueves por una nueva oleada de falsas amenazas de bombas contra una veintena de aviones. El episodio parece un acto coordinado en un momento especialmente turbulento en Europa, según observadores y expertos. Al menos 20 vuelos con destino a ciudades europeas —tres de ellos con origen o destino en Madrid— han sufrido este jueves falsos avisos de bomba que les han obligado a realizar aterrizajes de emergencia, sin contratiempos en todos los casos. Dos vuelos han sido desviados. Una de las aeronaves, con destino a Roma, ha sido escoltada por aviones militares italianos. Las incidencias, que investigan las autoridades nacionales, han afectado a aeropuertos de España, Francia, Italia, Bélgica, Bulgaria, Chequia, Rumania, Polonia y Austria. Suceden, además a dos días de falsas alertas en siete vuelos. Todos sobre el espacio aéreo europeo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: 7e étape du Tour du Faso 2026 : Anes Riahi offre la 4e victoire à l’Algérie
items.description: Anes Riahi a remporté, le 5 novembre 2026, la 7 e étape du Tour du Faso 2026. Etape courue entre Ouagadougou et Pô, l’Algérien a bouclé les 143km76 en 3h12mn33s à une vitesse moyenne de 44,796km/h. Le Sud-africain Gustav Basson conserve le maillot jaune. Après le triplé de Yacine Hamza, l’Algérie signe sa 4 e victoire d’étape sur le 37 e tour cycliste international du Faso. Le jeudi 5 novembre 2026, Anes Riahi a remporté la 7 e étape courue entre Ouagadougou et Pô. Longue de 143km76, l’Algérien a franchi la ligne d’arrivée en 3h12mn33s à une vitesse moyenne de 44,796 km/h. Comme au départ de l’étape précédente, ils étaient 70 coureurs sur la ligne. Peloton groupé pendant une vingtaine de km, la course prend une autre configuration avec une groupe d’échappée au Km28 à l’approche du premier point chaud à Kombissiri. Neuf au total, il était composé de trois Burkinabè de l’équipe régionale du Centre (Moucaila Rawendé, Mohamadi Ilboudo et Pawendin Bamouni), deux Marocains (Mohcine El Kouraji et Youssef Bdadou), deux Algériens (Anes Riahi et Hamza Amari), un néerlandais (Jonathan Kerkhofs) et un Camerounais (Ibrahim Mouhammed). Avec un écart de 1mn28s avec le peloton, le groupe d’échappée franchi le premier point chaud, au K39,84. A ce sprint intermédiaire, Anes Riahi s’impose devant Youssef Bdadou et Mohamadi Ilboudo. Au fil de la course, le groupe des fuyards creuse d’avantage d’écart. Il s’accroit jusqu’à 3mn22s au Km60 à la porte du 2 e sprint intermédiaire. Là encore l’Algérien, Anes Riahi est de nouveau rendez-vous. Il s’impose respectivement devant Mohcine El Kouraji et Moucaila Rawendé. Très inspiré, le groupe de tête met d’avantage du rythme à la course. L’écart qui était de 3mn22s avec le peloton, s’accroit et atteint 5mn15s à l’arrivée du 3 e point chaud à Nobéré au Km99,63. Comme à l’arrivée des deux précédents sprint intermédiaire, Anes Riahi fait encore parler de sa puissance pour son triplé. Mené par l’Algérien, le groupe des fuyards met le cap sur Pô. Malgré la réduction de l’écart le groupe d’échappée est à l’arrivée à Pô. Anes Riahi confirme sa forme et s’impose en autoritaire et offre la 4 e victoire d’étape à l’Algérie. Il devance respectivement le Marocain, Youssef Bdadou et le Néerlandais, Jonathan Kerkhofs. Leader depuis la 4 e étape, Gustav Basson est en jaune à l’arrivée à Pô. Tout comme le Sud-Africain, Yacine Hamza de l’Algérien conserve le maillot vert par point. Le maillot du meilleur demeure lla propriété du Burkinabè de l’équipe nationale, Soumaila Ilboudo. Le Marocain Youssef Bdadou est toujours propriétaire du maillot des points chaud. Celui du premier des burkinabè est revenu à Moukaila Rawendé de l’équipe nationale du Burkina. Ollo Aimé Césaire HIEN

items.title: 2027: Court ruling strategy to weaken my support in north – Atiku
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using Thursday’s Federal High Court judgment on the leadership of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the opposition party’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections. Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region. In a statement on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former vice president insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country. He said the Sokoto reception reflected Nigerians’ growing frustration with economic hardship and their desire for a change of government. “The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said. Rejecting attempts to frame his candidacy as a Northern project, Atiku said the economic crisis confronting Nigerians had made his political message relevant across regional boundaries. “My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. There is a difference between being from the North and being a candidate only for the North. Hunger and hardship do not respect regional boundaries. Nigerians across the country are suffering under this government, and they deserve a leader with a credible plan to make life affordable again,” he said. Atiku alleged that the judgment was intended to disrupt the momentum of his campaign and weaken the opposition’s growing political reach. “The timing of this judgment is no coincidence. It is part of a strategy to weaken my support in the North and frustrate a campaign whose message is resonating across the country. But the ruling party’s greatest miscalculation is to assume that my support ends in the North. What we saw in Sokoto, what we will see in Kebbi and across the country, is the strength of a national movement,” he said. On the legal implications, Atiku questioned why the leadership dispute was reopened despite an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025. He said the court had dismissed the challenge to the David Mark-led leadership after upholding objections bordering on jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies, adding that the substantive issues were also resolved in favour of the defendants. “Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute? This is a calculated attempt to circumvent a subsisting judgment. We will challenge this judicial manoeuvre at the Court of Appeal,” he said. The former Vice President urged ADC supporters to remain peaceful and law-abiding, insisting that the court ruling would not interrupt the party’s mobilisation. “Our journey to rescue Nigeria from the hardship imposed by the APC government is a long one. Our Affordable Life campaign will continue because Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis,” he said. items.title: Essaouira Fashion Week : une première pour la Fête de l’Unité
items.description: Défilé sur la plage, collections présentées à la Skala, créateurs marocains et français : Essaouira accueille, les 6 et 7 novembre, la première édition de l’Essaouira Fashion Week, placée sous le signe de la Fête de l’Unité. La ville d’Essaouira s’apprête à vivre, les 6 et 7 novembre 2026, la première édition de l’Essaouira Fashion Week. Programmé à l’occasion de la Fête de l’Unité et du 51ᵉ anniversaire de la Marche Verte, ce rendez-vous rassemblera des créateurs et des talents venus du Maroc et de France. L’événement est organisé en partenariat avec l’association « Mogador, ville de la mode », l’Institut français, l’Ambassade de France au Maroc et le Forum euro-méditerranéen des jeunes leaders. Cet attelage d’acteurs associatifs, culturels et diplomatiques donne à cette première édition une dimension résolument tournée vers l’échange entre les deux rives. Les festivités s’ouvriront le 6 novembre par un défilé inaugural organisé sur la plage d’Essaouira. Cette soirée d’ouverture sera accompagnée de prestations équestres, conçues comme un hommage aux pionniers de la Marche Verte et aux valeurs d’unité nationale. La mode et la mémoire collective se retrouveront ainsi réunies sur le sable de la cité des alizés. Le lendemain, l’événement prendra ses quartiers à la Skala de la médina, inscrite au patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO. Des collections marocaines et françaises y seront présentées dans un cadre ouvert sur l’océan Atlantique, entre remparts historiques et horizon marin. Au-delà du spectacle, les organisateurs assignent à l’Essaouira Fashion Week une double mission. Elle vise d’abord à mettre en lumière les jeunes talents et à renforcer les échanges créatifs entre le Maroc, l’Afrique et l’Europe. Elle entend ensuite ouvrir des perspectives professionnelles aux jeunes dans les domaines du design, de l’industrie, de l’image et de la communication. Cette première édition ambitionne en outre de poser les bases d’un rendez-vous annuel où création et jeunesse se rencontrent, et de célébrer l’identité marocaine dans sa dimension africaine, tout en apportant une nouvelle dimension au paysage culturel d’Essaouira. Cette ambition a été portée par Othman Chic, directeur de production de l’événement. Dans une déclaration à la presse, il a affirmé : « L’Essaouira Fashion Week n’est pas seulement un défilé de mode, c’est un engagement envers les jeunes de notre ville et de notre pays. » Il a ajouté que les organisateurs souhaitaient faire des rencontres entre professionnels et talents émergents le point de départ de possibilités concrètes de formation, d’accompagnement et de stages. À terme, ils ambitionnent de contribuer à faire d’Essaouira un pôle de la mode africaine, fier de son identité et ouvert sur le monde. Sur le plan artistique, la programmation de cette première édition fera dialoguer différentes approches de la création. La créatrice française Louise Marcaud y présentera une vision contemporaine et responsable de la mode. De son côté, la marque marocaine « Anouri Original » proposera une réinterprétation des tapis traditionnels dans des créations actuelles, entre héritage artisanal et esthétique d’aujourd’hui. items.title: Agence Faso Mêbo : Le Ministère en charge de l’Agriculture remet des matériaux d’une valeur de 32 millions de FCFA
items.description: Le Ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques (MAERH) a procédé, ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, à une remise de matériaux au profit de l’Agence Faso Mêbo. Évalué à 32 millions de FCFA, ce don est composé de granite, de poubelles et d’huile de décoffrage. À travers cette initiative, le département entend contribuer au renforcement des moyens matériels de l’Agence et soutenir ses activités sur le terrain. L'agence Faso Mêbo se frotte les mains par un renfort de taille. En effet, le Ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques (MAERH) a effectué un don d'un coût global de 32 millions de FCFA. Il est composé de 20 millions de FCFA pour les poubelles et de 12 millions de FCFA pour le granite et les huiles destinées à la confection des moules. Le Colonel-major Alassane Guira expliquant l'origine de ce geste Ce geste s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’accompagnement des initiatives nationales de développement et de construction. Les matériaux remis devraient ainsi permettre à l’Agence Faso Mêbo de renforcer ses capacités opérationnelles dans la réalisation de ses missions. Au nom du personnel du ministère, le Directeur de cabinet du ministre d'État, ministre en charge des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le Colonel-major Alassane Guira, a procédé à la remise de cette contribution. Il a expliqué que ce geste traduit l'adhésion des 8 000 agents du département à la vision du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, qui place l'engagement patriotique et citoyen au cœur de la construction nationale. Le personnel du Ministère donnant un coup de main à Faso Mêbo Selon lui, cette contribution entend accompagner les trois principales dimensions de la mission de Faso Mêbo. « La première concerne le désenclavement des villes et des campagnes. À cet effet, nous avons mis à la disposition de l'agence Faso Mêbo 440 tonnes de granite destinées aux travaux d'aménagement. La deuxième dimension porte sur l’embellissement et l'assainissement du cadre de vie ; à cela, nous avons offert 500 poubelles. Enfin, par ce geste, nous ambitionnons de contribuer à la mobilisation citoyenne et au développement endogène, troisième volet de l'action de Faso Mêbo », a déclaré le Directeur de cabinet du ministre d'État, ministre en charge de l'Agriculture. Un aperçu des huiles… Tout en affirmant que l'engagement doit se traduire par des actes concrets, il a souligné que « le patriotisme se traduit et se démontre par les actes. Certes, des discours peuvent venir enrober cela, mais l'essentiel pour nous, c'est de poser les actes ». Par ailleurs, M. Guira a ajouté que la construction nationale relève d'une responsabilité collective et individuelle, invitant ainsi chaque Burkinabè à apporter sa contribution, selon ses moyens et de manière volontaire, au développement du pays. Un aperçu des poubelles Nadège KINDA Minute.bf

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le personnel du MAERAH apporte 32 millions de F CFA en matériel à Faso Mêbo
items.description: Le personnel du ministère de l'Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques (MAERAH) a fait un don de matériel d'une valeur de 32 millions de F CFA à l'Agence Faso Mêbo, ce 5 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Le don est composé de 440 tonnes de granite, de 500 poubelles et de bidons d'huile pour la confection des pavés. Il constitue la réponse de l'ensemble du personnel du ministère à la vision du président du Faso. Cette vision met l'accent sur la mobilisation citoyenne et l'engagement patriotique pour bâtir souverainement le Burkina Faso, selon le colonel-major Alassane Guiré, directeur de cabinet du ministère en charge de l’Agriculture. « Nous sommes là ce matin sur instruction du ministre d'État en charge de l'Agriculture, et cela au nom de l'ensemble de la communauté de femmes et d'hommes, près de 8 000 agents qui constituent notre ministère et qui ont donc voulu traduire leur entière adhésion à la vision du camarade président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, qui a donc opté de placer le développement, l'engagement patriotique et la mobilisation citoyenne au cœur du développement de notre pays, pour la construction de notre nation, pour que nous ayons une nation souveraine, prospère et solidaire », a-t-il indiqué. Le personnel du ministère chargé de l'Agriculture veut ainsi accompagner l'Agence Faso Mêbo dans l'atteinte de ses différentes missions. En offrant ce granite, les agents se disent convaincus qu'il servira à aménager des voies afin de désenclaver les villes et les campagnes du pays. Pour le volet embellissement et assainissement, l'installation de poubelles dans les rues permettra d'atteindre l'objectif visé. Le directeur de cabinet a ajouté que la mobilisation citoyenne dont le personnel a fait preuve vient donner tout son sens aux discours d'engagement patriotique. « Nous avons la conviction que cette nation, nous avons tous la responsabilité citoyenne et individuelle de contribuer à son développement. Ce n'est pas l'État qui doit porter le développement de cette nation, c'est l'ensemble des Burkinabè de façon individuelle et de façon volontaire qui doivent donc apporter leur contribution », a ajouté le colonel-major Alassane Guiré. Au-delà du don, le personnel a prêté main-forte aux travailleurs du site. Ils ont pu découvrir les étapes de la confection des pavés, du mélange des agrégats au nettoyage et au remplissage des moules pour en faire sortir plusieurs types de pavés. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le personnel du MAERAH apporte 32 millions de F CFA en matériel à Faso Mêbo est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Court ruling: Don’t set Nigeria on fire over 2027 – ADC to APC
items.description: …warns against using courts to cripple opposition By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has warned the All Progressives Congress (APC) against setting Nigeria on fire in its desperation to retain power in 2027, accusing the ruling party of using the judiciary to cripple the opposition and undermine democratic competition. The party issued the warning after a Federal High Court judgment in Abuja which it said threatens its leadership and the candidacy of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar. It argued that the implications extend beyond its leadership, potentially affecting thousands of candidates seeking elective offices across the country. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC linked the timing of the judgment by Justice Peter Lifu, barely 24 hours after its massive presidential campaign rally in Sokoto, to what it described as the APC’s growing desperation over the opposition’s rising political profile. “We have reasons to believe that the judgment had long been written on this case. The Sokoto rally was simply a trigger that stampeded its delivery,” Abdullahi alleged. The party warned that the dispute was not merely about the political fortunes of Senator David Mark or Atiku, but the right of its candidates to participate in the 2027 elections. “Do these people understand what they are playing with? This is not about Atiku Abubakar or David Mark. It is about the democratic rights of Nigerians to freely choose their own leaders. It is about the rights of thousands of candidates to participate in a democratic process,” the statement said. To challenge the judgment, the ADC cited an earlier ruling by Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, delivered on July 2, 2026, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025, which it said affirmed the legitimacy of the David Mark-led National Working Committee (NWC) and directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise the leadership. The party argued that a court of coordinate jurisdiction could not sit on appeal over, review, vary or nullify a subsisting judgment of another court of equal jurisdiction. “The ADC, therefore, rejects any consequential orders founded on a determination that appears to disregard these fundamental legal principles. However, we await the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the said judgment to ascertain its precise terms, scope and operative orders,” Abdullahi stated. The ADC accused the APC of repeating what it called a familiar pattern of using judicial controversies to frustrate opposition whenever it gains political momentum, warning that the struggle to retain power must not come at the expense of national stability. “We warn the APC: do not play with fires you cannot control. The peace and stability of Nigeria are bigger than the ambition of any president or political party. Nobody should be so desperate to retain power that they are prepared to put the entire country at risk,” the party warned. Challenging President Bola Tinubu and the APC to face the electorate, Abdullahi questioned why a government confident in its performance and popularity would fear a competitive election. “If the President thinks he has performed well in office, why is he afraid of competition? If the APC thinks that its policies and candidates are popular, why don’t they subject themselves to free and fair elections?” he asked. The party called on the judiciary not to allow itself to be used to foist dictatorship on Nigeria, insisting that the controversy was bigger than the ADC or Atiku. It urged its members nationwide to remain calm and law-abiding while it pursues all available legal remedies. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s five great moments with Portugal
items.description: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday to bring down the curtain on more than two decades in the Portugal shirt. He scored a record 146 times in a mammoth 234 appearances for his country having made his debut in 2003. Here are his five stand-out games with the Selecao. 2013: Outclassing Zlatan Having won the World Cup play-off first leg 1-0 against Sweden thanks to the iconic No. 7, Portugal headed to Stockholm for the return fixture. Ronaldo opened the scoring before Zlatan Ibrahimovic brought the sides level in the tie with a double in the Swedish capital. But the then Real Madrid attacker claimed Portugal’s spot at the tournament in Brazil by completing his hat-trick in two minutes. 2016: Tears before the joy Portugal reached the Euro 2016 final having failed to win a single group game. Ronaldo’s side went into the decider against hosts France in Paris searching for their first major international trophy and to make up for the past after losing to Greece on home soil 12 years earlier. The forward left the field injured and in tears after just 25 minutes before spending the rest of the game on the touchline cheering on his teammates. Eder scored the winner in extra-time to the relief of Ronaldo and 11 million Portuguese compatriots. 2018: One-man mission Fresh from winning three straight Champions Leagues with Real, Ronaldo faced Spain in Portugal’s World Cup opener in 2018. CR7 opened the scoring in Sochi with a penalty before grabbing a hat-trick, including a superb late free kick, to fire Portugal to a thrilling draw. 2025: 40 years young Three months after turning 40, Ronaldo helped Portugal to the Nations League final against Spain in Munich. He scored the winner over Germany in the semi-final before claiming the equaliser against Spain to send the decider to extra time. The Selecao eventually won on penalties, six years on from winning the same crown. 2026: Outplayed Croatia Following a lacklustre group stage, Ronaldo and Portugal faced Croatia in the last 32 of this year’s World Cup in Toronto. Despite the prospect of it being his final ever World Cup match, Ronaldo took control of things. He had an early effort chalked off for offside and Ivan Perisic put Croatia ahead, but Ronaldo equalised for Portugal from the penalty spot. Goncalo Ramos’ late header gave Portugal a memorable 2-1 victory and sent them into the last 16, where they lost to eventual winners Spain. items.title: Bank of England lifts rate for first time since 2023 to fight inflation
items.description: The Bank of England (BoE) raised its benchmark interest rate to four per cent on Thursday, the first increase in more than three years, as soaring energy costs push up global inflation. The central bank tightened borrowing costs by a quarter point, catching up with the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank in lifting rates since the start of the Middle East conflict . Along with Ukraine’s strikes on Russian refineries, disruptions to Gulf energy supplies owing to the US-Iran war have caused record-high diesel prices around the world. “There is now enough inflationary pressure in the pipeline caused by the rise in energy prices that an increase in Bank Rate is warranted,” BoE governor Andrew Bailey said in a statement. “Today’s increase shouldn’t be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes,” Bailey said. “But, unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase.” Despite surging inflation, the bank upgraded its forecasts for UK economic growth in 2026 and 2027. The central bank now estimates gross domestic product to hit 1.6pc this year and 1.3pc next year. In July, it had forecast GDP growth of 1.1pc in both years. The BoE last raised its key interest rate in August 2023, and has kept the cost of borrowing at 3.75pc since December. Britain’s annual inflation rate accelerated by more than expected in September, rising to 3.5 percent — well above the bank’s target of two percent. The BoE on Thursday said its central forecast saw UK inflation peaking at 4.9pc in the second quarter of next year. Millions of Britons face a jump in energy bills from the start of 2027, even after the government offered some assistance in its annual budget announcement last week.

items.title: Tour du Faso 2026: l’Algérien Anes Riahi s’impose à Pô et offre une quatrième victoire à son pays
items.description: L’Algérie poursuit sa belle moisson sur les routes du 37e Tour cycliste international du Faso. Son coureur Anes Riahi a remporté, ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026, la 7e étape de la compétition, disputée entre Ouagadougou et Pô sur une distance de 143,76 km. Ce nouveau succès porte à quatre le nombre de victoires d’étape décrochées par les Algériens dans cette édition. La délégation algérienne continue de faire parler d’elle sur le Tour du Faso 2026. Ce jeudi, Anes Riahi a franchi en tête la ligne d’arrivée à Pô, au terme des 143,76 km reliant la capitale burkinabè à cette localité du Centre-Sud. Grâce à cette performance, le coureur algérien confirme la bonne dynamique de son équipe dans cette 37e édition du rendez-vous cycliste international. Il permet également à son pays d'enregistrer une quatrième victoire d’étape depuis le début de la compétition. items.title: Gombe @ 30: ‘I’m Overwhelmed by Inuwa Yahaya’s Urban Renewal, Development Projects’ –Orji
items.description: -Former Military Administrator applauds governor’s regional leadership, inspects mega projects, recalls Gombe’s formative years By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe Thirty years after he presided over the formative administration of Gombe State following its creation on October 1, 1996, the Pioneer Military Administrator, Group Captain Joseph I. Orji (rtd.), has returned to a state whose expanding urban landscape, monumental infrastructure and emerging economic profile have left him visibly impressed. Orji, who spent five days in Gombe as part of activities marking the state’s 30th anniversary, expressed overwhelming admiration for the infrastructural transformation under Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, describing the scale of urban renewal and development projects as remarkable. For the former military administrator, who supervised the affairs of the newly created state between October 1, 1996, and August 6, 1998, the visit offered a rare opportunity to reconnect with the foundations he helped establish and assess how successive administrations have shaped Gombe’s development trajectory. His assessment was particularly significant against the backdrop of the state’s journey from its modest beginnings three decades ago to its present status as an emerging administrative, commercial and investment destination in the North-East. Speaking after commissioning six completed executive residential buildings at the Government House, Gombe, on October 27, 2026, Orji said he was overwhelmed by the scale of development initiatives undertaken by the Inuwa Yahaya administration. “I’m overwhelmed by the spirit of urban renewal and what I have seen. I should say that I have been positively confused. I’m so proud, and I’m so happy to be here with you,” he declared. The former administrator’s remarks reflected not only his admiration for the physical transformation of the state capital but also his appreciation of the governor’s deliberate efforts to strengthen Gombe’s institutional capacity, economic competitiveness and regional relevance. Six executive residences reinforce regional hospitality: One of the major highlights of Orji’s visit was the commissioning of six executive residential buildings at the Government House, named after the six states of the North-East geopolitical zone. The facilities were conceived to provide befitting accommodation for visiting governors, senior government officials and other high-profile personalities attending official engagements in Gombe. Constructed and furnished with modern facilities, including elevators and other essential amenities, the buildings represent an investment in the state’s hospitality infrastructure and its ambition to strengthen intergovernmental relations. The Commissioner for Housing and Urban Development, Muhammad Sa’idu Fawu, disclosed that construction commenced in November 2023 and was completed in February 2025. He said the buildings had been fully furnished and equipped to guarantee comfort, convenience and security for their occupants. Governor Inuwa Yahaya explained that the project was designed to provide appropriate accommodation for visiting dignitaries while reinforcing Gombe’s traditional hospitality and its strategic position as a meeting point for the six North-Eastern states. The governor also said the initiative reflected his administration’s determination to preserve the vision of the state’s founding fathers while consolidating the institutional and developmental foundations established by successive administrations. Describing Gombe as the “Jewel in the Savannah”, Orji commended the governor for recognising that the state’s development must extend beyond its geographical boundaries. “Gombe is a Jewel in the Savannah, and you are providing that leadership and shelter to others,” he said. He particularly applauded the governor’s efforts at promoting regional unity, cooperation and stronger relationships among the six North-Eastern states, noting that Gombe’s strategic location and hospitality could serve as catalysts for regional integration. From Government House to emerging economic corridors: Beyond the commissioning ceremony, Orji’s five-day inspection tour provided an opportunity to assess the breadth of infrastructural development taking place across Gombe State. Accompanied by the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Hon. Shehu Yerima Abdullahi, the former administrator inspected several completed and ongoing projects in the state capital and other strategic locations. Members of the inspection team included the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Works and Infrastructure, Danladi Adamu; Director of Civil Engineering, Engr. Abubakar Musa; and Director of Building, Ministry of Housing and Urban Development, Arc. Ahmed Yahaya. Among the projects inspected were the new Deputy Governor’s Office, Emirs and Chiefs Secretariat, New High Court Complex, the underpass linking the Three Arms Zone with Shehu Abubakar District and several road networks within the mega city centre. He also visited the new House of Assembly Complex and the Ultra-modern State Secretariat Complex, facilities designed to strengthen legislative and administrative operations while providing a more conducive working environment for public servants. Other projects included the 550 Family Homes Estate and its connecting road network to Tumfure, the ongoing Agro-Livestock Development Zone and the Muhammadu Buhari Industrial Park. The inspection further took him to the multi-billion-naira Machanic Village and Dankwambo Mega Motor Park, two strategic projects expected to strengthen commercial activities, transportation and the state’s economic base. Inuwa Yahaya Builds, Equips NYSC Orientation Camp in Boltongo In another significant milestone in the infrastructure development drive of the Gombe State Government as part of activities marking the 30th anniversary of the state’s creation, the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya has constructed and furnished a modern National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) Orientation Camp in Boltongo, Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area. The purpose-built facility represents a major investment in youth development and institutional infrastructure, designed to provide a conducive environment for the orientation, training and welfare of corps members posted to Gombe State for their mandatory one-year national service. The camp is equipped with separate and adequate hostel accommodation for male and female corps members, a functional water reticulation system, an internal road network, administrative blocks, a dining hall, a lecture theatre and residential quarters for staff. The entire facility is also secured with perimeter fencing to ensure safety and order within the camp. Beyond its impressive physical structures, the project reflects the state government’s commitment to improving the welfare and living conditions of young Nigerians who are deployed to Gombe to serve their fatherland. For corps members, the availability of decent accommodation, reliable water supply, accessible internal roads and purpose-built training facilities will significantly enhance their orientation experience and provide a more comfortable atmosphere throughout their stay in the state. The completion of the camp is therefore not merely an addition to Gombe infrastructure portfolio but also a strategic investment in youth development, national integration and the success of the NYSC scheme. As Gombe marks three decades of statehood, the NYSC Orientation Camp in Boltongo stands out as one of the administration’s enduring contributions to institutional development, while reinforcing the state’s readiness to welcome and provide a hospitable environment for young Nigerians from different parts of the country. These projects collectively reflects the administration’s approach to development, which places emphasis on urban renewal, institutional infrastructure, industrialisation, commercial expansion and the creation of an enabling environment for private-sector investment. Dadinkowa Superhighway: Gombe’s strategic regional connection. A particularly significant aspect of the inspection tour was Orji’s visit to the Dadinkowa corridor, where the proposed superhighway alignment is expected to connect Gombe and the six North-Eastern states to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. The project has strategic implications for regional transportation, trade, investment and economic integration, particularly for a North-Eastern region whose vast agricultural and commercial potentials require efficient transportation infrastructure. Governor Inuwa Yahaya’s engagements and lobbying efforts with President Bola Tinubu were instrumental in securing approval for the Gombe alignment, including the proposed adjustment of the Sokoto highway corridor to accommodate the connection. The development represents an important intervention in positioning Gombe as a strategic transportation link between the North-East and the broader national highway network. For a state that has consistently sought to leverage its geographical advantage, the proposed connection could open new opportunities for agricultural marketing, movement of goods, industrial development and private investment. Dadinkowa hydropower and industrialisation drive: Orji’s inspection also covered the Dadinkowa Hydroelectric Power project, whose contribution to electricity generation and industrial development forms part of Gombe’s broader economic development strategy. Of particular interest is the utilisation of power from the facility to support electricity supply to the Muhammadu Buhari Industrial Park, where the state government is pursuing an industrialisation agenda aimed at attracting manufacturing and agro-processing enterprises. The industrial park is expected to serve as a major platform for transforming the state’s agricultural and mineral resources into finished products, generating employment and expanding economic activities. According to information made available during the inspection, 14 industrial concerns have taken positions at the park, signalling growing private-sector interest in the state’s investment drive. Among the companies is Agro Seedlings, backed by former President Olusegun Obasanjo, which has commenced production. The development is significant because the success of industrial parks depends not merely on the provision of land and infrastructure but also on the ability to attract functional businesses capable of creating jobs, stimulating local supply chains and contributing to economic growth. The emergence of these industrial concerns therefore represents an important step in Gombe’s effort to move beyond a predominantly public-sector-driven economy towards a more diversified productive base. Education and institutional development across the state. Another important dimension of Orji’s inspection tour was his visit to major educational institutions, reflecting the importance of education in the state’s development over the past three decades. The institutions visited included Gombe State University (with campuses in Dukku (Faculty of Environmental sciences) and Malam Sidi (Faculty of Agriculture), Gombe State Polytechnic, Bajoga, State College of Education, Billiri, College for Legal Studies, Nafada, College of Nursing Sciences, Gombe and College of Health Sciences and Technology, Kaltungo. The institutions represent important pillars of human capital development, professional training and manpower production for Gombe and the wider North-Eastern region. Their growth and expansion also demonstrate how the state has progressively invested in educational infrastructure to widen access to tertiary education and develop the skilled workforce required to support its administrative, commercial and industrial aspirations. For Orji, whose administration operated during the challenging formative years of the state, the expansion of educational institutions and other public facilities offered an opportunity to appreciate the distance Gombe has travelled since its creation. APC inaugurates campaign councils: Orji’s anniversary visit also coincided with significant political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. On October 29, 2026, the former military administrator joined other dignitaries at the International Conference Centre, Gombe, to witness the inauguration of the Gombe State All Progressives Congress (APC) Advisory Council, Campaign Council and Women’s Campaign Council. The event attracted party leaders, stakeholders, council members and supporters from across the state, marking the formal commencement of the councils’ activities towards coordinating the party’s political engagement, reconciliation and grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. The inauguration formed part of the political engagements surrounding the 30th anniversary celebrations, with party leaders reaffirming their commitment to strengthening the party’s structures and promoting unity among its members. Igbo Community Honours piyoneer Administrator: Beyond official ceremonies, project inspections and political engagements, one of the most emotionally significant moments of Orji’s visit was the special reception organised in his honour by the Igbo Community Welfare Association (ICWA), Gombe. The reception, held at Mar-Cornel Resort Hotel, Gombe, brought together prominent Igbo sons and daughters residing in the state to celebrate a man they described as one of the architects of Gombe’s formative history. Organised in collaboration with the Special Adviser on Inter-Community Relations, Hon. Cornelius Ewuzie, the gathering attracted members of the Igbo community, the Council of Chiefs and other distinguished personalities. The delegation of the Igbo Delegates Assembly (IDA), representing 19 Northern states and the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, was led by its President-General, Chief Kenneth Okeugo. Also present were the Chairman of the Council of Chiefs, Chief Michael Ogbonna; President-General of ICWA, Barrister Herbert N. Nwoye; and other community leaders. Speakers at the event described Orji as a legend, father figure and builder whose contributions to Gombe’s establishment and early development remain indelible. They recalled that his administration laid important foundations for governance and infrastructural development at a time when the newly created state faced considerable financial and administrative challenges. Among the projects attributed to his administration were 25 three-bedroom residential units at Buhari Estate, 80 housing units along Bauchi Road, low-cost housing accommodation for junior workers and the High Court Complex, alongside other foundational administrative and infrastructural initiatives. The speakers particularly recalled that these projects were undertaken despite the reported absence of a dedicated take-off grant for the newly created state. For the Igbo community, the reception was more than a ceremonial celebration. It was an opportunity to acknowledge a pioneer administrator whose early leadership, they said, helped establish an environment in which non-indigenes could participate meaningfully in the social, economic and political development of Gombe. They noted that the foundations laid during his tenure contributed to a sense of belonging, dignity and participation among residents from different ethnic backgrounds. In their separate remarks, community leaders reaffirmed the commitment of Ndigbo in Gombe to peaceful coexistence, inter-communal harmony and the continued development of the state. The gathering was marked by nostalgia, solidarity and renewed appreciation of the historical relationship between Orji and the people of Gombe. Orji Urges Ndi Igbo to Promote Peaceful Coexistence, Support APC Government. As part of activities marking the 30th anniversary of the creation of Gombe State, the Pioneer Military Administrator, Group Captain Joseph Orji (rtd.), has called on members of the Igbo community resident in the state to sustain peaceful coexistence with their host communities and support the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya. Orji, who made the appeal while responding to speeches at an event commemorating the state’s 30th anniversary, emphasised the importance of mutual respect, understanding and adherence to the cultural values, traditions and customs of host communities. He urged the Ndi Igbo to avoid actions capable of generating misunderstandings, friction or strained relationships with their host communities, stressing that peaceful coexistence remained fundamental to unity, stability and sustainable development. The former Military Administrator also encouraged the Igbo community to identify with and support the APC-led administration in Gombe State, noting that such cooperation would further strengthen the existing cordial relationship between the government and the people, as well as consolidate the bonds of friendship and mutual understanding among residents. He maintained that the continued development of Gombe State depended largely on the collective commitment of its diverse ethnic groups to peaceful coexistence, cooperation and support for government policies and programmes. Thirty years of statehood: From foundation to transformation. Orji’s return to Gombe, three decades after he played a defining role in its establishment, provided a unique historical perspective on the state’s development journey. The contrast between the Gombe of 1996 and the expanding state capital of 2026 is evident in its growing network of roads, modern government facilities, educational institutions, residential estates, industrial infrastructure and emerging investment corridors. His visit also highlighted the contributions of successive administrations in consolidating the foundations laid by the pioneer leadership and responding to the changing needs of a growing population. Under Governor Inuwa Yahaya, the development agenda has increasingly focused on urban renewal, regional connectivity, institutional expansion, industrialisation and the mobilisation of private-sector investment. Yet, as Gombe celebrates 30 years of statehood, the significance of the anniversary goes beyond the commissioning of projects and the presentation of infrastructural achievements. It also presents an opportunity to examine how effectively these investments translate into improved living standards, sustainable employment, stronger institutions, economic productivity and better public services for ordinary residents. For Orji, however, the opportunity to return to the state he helped establish and witness its transformation was evidently a moment of pride and fulfilment. His assessment of the Inuwa Yahaya administration, particularly its commitment to urban renewal, regional cooperation and strategic infrastructure, underscored the importance of continuity in governance and the preservation of development visions across successive administrations. As Gombe moves beyond its third decade, the challenge before its leadership and people is to sustain the momentum, deepen economic diversification, strengthen public institutions and ensure that the benefits of development reach communities across the state. For the Pioneer Administrator, the Gombe he helped nurture in 1996 has clearly travelled a remarkable distance. His five-day return was, in many respects, a reunion with history and a firsthand encounter with a state steadily redefining its place in the North-East. items.title: Football : Cristiano Ronaldo annonce la fin de son aventure avec la sélection portugaise
items.description: Le Portugais Cristiano Ronaldo (CR7), 41 ans, a annoncé ce 5 novembre 2026 sa retraite international. « Aujourd’hui mon voyage avec la sélection nationale arrive à sa fin », a-t-il déclaré dans une vidéo publiée sur les réseaux sociaux. CR7 arrête avec la sélection portugaise après y avoir joué 234 matchs pour 146 buts sous le maillot portugais depuis 2003. Son discours complet : « À vous, Portugais, Le jour est arrivé de rendre le maillot numéro 7 de notre sélection, celle de nous tous. Je ne l'ai jamais considéré comme exclusivement le mien, mais pendant 23 ans, j'ai eu le privilège et la responsabilité de le porter, de le défendre et de l’emmener avec moi dans les stades du monde entier. Aujourd'hui, le moment est venu de le transmettre à l'avenir. Ce n'était pas une décision facile, car certaines décisions ne se prennent pas uniquement avec la tête, elles se prennent aussi avec le cœur. Un parcours commencé en août 2003 s'achève, un parcours qui a changé ma vie à jamais. Lorsque je regarde en arrière et que je repense à tout ce que j'ai vécu avec la sélection, je ne vois pas seulement des matchs, des buts, des records ou des trophées. Je vois des personnes. Je vois des immigrés qui, pendant 90 minutes, se sentaient un peu plus proches du Portugal. Je vois des millions de Portugais que je n'ai jamais rencontrés personnellement, mais qui ont fait partie de ma vie. Car au final, le football est bien plus qu'un simple jeu. Le football, ce sont les gens. Tout au long de ma carrière en sélection, j'ai toujours cherché à repousser mes limites. Je voulais gagner, je voulais être le meilleur, je voulais marquer l'histoire. J'ai toujours été exigeant envers moi-même. J'ai toujours voulu davantage, j'ai toujours cru que nous pouvions aller encore plus loin. Et j'ai tout donné pour ce maillot. Il y a eu des après-midi et des soirées parfaites, des victoires que je n'oublierai jamais, et des défaites dont le souvenir me fait encore mal aujourd'hui. J'ai aussi échoué, j'ai aussi souffert, il y a également eu des moments où je n'ai pas été capable d'offrir aux Portugais ce qu'ils désiraient tant. Mais je n'ai jamais abandonné. Et surtout, je n'ai jamais cessé d'être fier de représenter le Portugal. Au fil de ces années, j'ai appris des choses très simples. Les buts passent, les trophées restent dans les musées, les records finissent toujours par être battus. Mais il y a quelque chose que le temps ne pourra jamais effacer : la place que nous occupons dans le cœur des gens. Si je vous ai déjà rendu heureux, si l'un de mes buts vous a déjà fait prendre quelqu'un dans vos bras, oublier un souci ou ressentir de la fierté pour notre pays, alors tout cela en valait la peine. Car être Portugais, c'est aussi cela. Nous souffrons ensemble, nous nous relevons ensemble. Et nous y croyons à nouveau. Le Portugal aura toujours besoin de jeunes qui rêvent, de joueurs qui n'abandonnent jamais, de nouvelles générations qui croient qu'il est possible d'aller là où personne n'est encore allé. Car un pays qui continue de faire naître de nouveaux héros est un pays qui ne cesse jamais de croire en lui-même. À mes coéquipiers en sélection, je souhaite adresser un message particulier. Merci pour chaque course, pour chaque accolade, pour chaque discussion, pour chaque silence avant d'entrer sur le terrain, pour chaque victoire que nous avons célébrée ensemble et pour chaque défaite qui nous a rendus plus forts. J'ai eu le privilège d'être votre capitaine. Mais un capitaine ne marche jamais seul. Et vous faites partie de mon histoire. À tous les entraîneurs, dirigeants, médecins, kinésithérapeutes, intendants, employés et à toutes les personnes qui ont travaillé à mes côtés au fil de ces années, je vous adresse mes remerciements. Beaucoup d'entre vous n'apparaissent jamais sur les photos. Mais sans vous, aucune de ces photos n'aurait été possible. À ma famille, merci d'avoir partagé ce rêve avec moi. Merci d'avoir compris mes absences, les sacrifices et les moments où la sélection a dû occuper une place qui vous appartenait également. Si je suis allé aussi loin, c'est parce que nous avons toujours avancé main dans la main. Et à vous, les Portugais, à tous les Portugais dispersés aux quatre coins du monde, je souhaite dire une dernière chose. Il y a une image que je garderai toujours avec moi. Le moment où retentit l'hymne national. Je regarde autour de moi, je vois mes coéquipiers, je vois les tribunes, je vois des enfants, des mères, des pères et des grands-parents, je vois des Portugais qui ont parcouru tant de kilomètres simplement pour être là. Et pendant ces quelques minutes, nous cessons d'être différents. Il n'y a plus de clubs, il n'y a plus de couleurs, il n'y a plus de classes sociales, il n'y a plus de professions, il n'y a plus d'opinions. Il n'existe qu'une seule passion. Le Portugal. C'est ce sentiment que j’emporterai avec moi pour le reste de ma vie. Aujourd'hui, je mets fin à mon parcours sur le terrain avec la sélection nationale, je pars la tête haute, fier du chemin parcouru et avec la conscience d'avoir tout donné pour le Portugal. Mais je ne cesserai jamais d'être l'un des vôtres. Je continuerai à souffrir, à vibrer et à célébrer chaque victoire du Portugal avec vous. J'ai consacré ma vie à travailler pour devenir le meilleur joueur du monde. Aujourd'hui, je comprends que ma plus grande victoire a été d'avoir eu le mérite de représenter le meilleur pays du monde. Merci pour ces 23 années. Merci d'avoir cru en moi. Merci de m'avoir permis de vivre un rêve qui a commencé lorsque je n'étais encore qu'un enfant, à Madère, courant derrière un ballon. Le maillot numéro 7 reste. La fierté de l'avoir porté m'appartiendra pour toujours. Le Portugal sera toujours en moi. À jamais. Cristiano Ronaldo ». items.title: What I Lost to Shock Therapy—And What I Got Back
items.description: T he art therapist said to draw an emotional biography of your illness. The nurses gave the patients only four colors of crayon. After some deliberation, I drew my girlfriend in blue, then used red and orange to make the fires in California. I sketched my sister, Jane, rocking an approximation of her baby, Theo—whom I’d never met—in her arms. All of the faces were coming out wrong: angry and put upon, as if to say, I cannot sanction what he’s doing with my likeness . It was my third day in the psych ward, and I knew vaguely that my first electroconvulsive-therapy treatment was scheduled for the next day. But on the ward, the concept of time tended to blur. All I could say was that at some point, a nurse would affix electrodes to my temples and a doctor would begin inducing seizures. They’d keep zapping me until my agitated depression began to recede. And if those seizures didn’t work? I might have to get pretty comfy in art classes like this one. If you spend enough time seriously depressed, you’re fundamentally aware of ECT buzzing in the distance. At least it’s not ECT , you say about this ineffectual drug or that ineffectual therapist. Or Well, there’s always ECT , when that drug or therapy doesn’t take. You probably don’t talk about it much, because it freaks people out. But privately, you know. By May 2021, I’d spent a year descending into ever tighter spirals of despair. Somehow I’d held on at work, fooling the bosses that I was still a human being. But all the time, my best friends and girlfriend had hugged me and grown more and more afraid as I cycled through different SSRIs and SNRIs, then tricyclic and tetracyclic antidepressants, and then, on the advice of my distressed psychiatrist, through ecstatically high doses of medically supervised intravenous ketamine. Nothing worked for long. In my diary, I noted with horror that my desperation to get better was making room for an equally desperate wish: that some swift and painless event would release me from this slow and painful thing that other people called life. Thus I’d consented to the sterile safety of the ward, where I stood the least chance of hurting myself. I was aware of the myths about ECT: It would cause brain damage, or at least sap the intellect; it was as much a punishment as a cure; it was the first step to a permanent tenure in the madhouse. All of this I knew to be nonsense. Yet I also understood that sustained treatment, especially of the most aggressive electroshock, can prevent the consolidation of short-term memory into long-term and, in some cases, can complicate memory going back months. I was already familiar with the unpleasant disorientation of memory loss, because the past several years had constituted my deepest episode in a long career of depression—and depression, it turns out, is one of the most common causes of lost memory. I’d resolved to keep the electricity at bay as long as I could. But the drugs weren’t working. Nothing was working. So, I had come to accept the risk—in principle. I was open to bartering my way toward some kind of future by trading away a few memories. It seemed a reasonable exchange at the time. I n modern neuroscience , researchers typically divide long-term human memory into two categories: explicit and implicit. The former is subdivided into episodic memory, which is your recollection of personal events (that home run you hit in third grade; your first kiss), and semantic memory, which is general information about the world (what language people speak in Brazil; the year of the Battle of Hastings). Under the implicit category, we find procedural memory, which comprises ingrained skills and motor memory (how to play the piano or ride a bike). During depression, the most notable memory loss tends to be episodic: factual autobiography. That’s because your episodic memory depends on a well-functioning hippocampus—which is a luxury that depressives don’t always have. In sustained periods of major depression, memory inhibition strikes in two ways: You form new memories less easily, and you lose some access to older memories. Neurologically, that makes sense. If your hippocampus is shrunken and lethargic, your ability to consolidate short-term memory into long-term memory diminishes precipitously. Psychologically and philosophically, it also makes sense. The monochrome dread that marks each day also blurs the days together; the depressive is prone to withdraw from social life, from a traditional clock, from a sense of time, from meaning. You might feel like the life you’re living is not your own; you might try not to pay it much attention. Small wonder that it’s hard to remember. In many people, depression is marked by the certainty that the condition will continue, that you will always feel like this. If you’ve also lost faith in your memory, despair will recur, and imagining any kind of a future will become doubly difficult. When memory and depression are at war, depression creates its own feedback loop that works to shut out memory, along with sense and wisdom. If, for example, you could fully remember and inhabit a memory of when you were well, brought joy to someone you loved, performed a triumphant concert with your band, or hiked to the top of a mountain, then you’d know in your bones that depression is, among other things, a lie. You’d know that you are not the lowest of creatures but, rather, a creature brought temporarily low, that some retrievable version of you is capable of meeting the comedy and tragedy of life in measure. Nearly a year before I stumbled into the ward, I was already noting a disarray in my ability to retain moments. These lapses began in small ways. Some days I would start composing an email to a colleague, then review my sent messages and find that I’d already conveyed the pertinent info that morning. Slowly, other things became harder to remember: when and with which band I’d played a concert at such and such a bar, or when I’d most recently seen my mother. Forgetfulness of this kind isn’t merely inconvenient. Quickly, it becomes existential. Even in the earliest stages, my memory loss meddled with my illusion of a stable self. Selfhood is, after all, largely a function of memory—a serialized story about who you are, based on who you’ve been and what you’ve done. [ Read: My life depends on playing chess 40 times a day ] In Nothing to Be Frightened Of , his 2008 memoir about the approach of death, Julian Barnes wrote, “Memory is identity. I have believed this since—oh, since I can remember. You are what you have done; what you have done is in your memory; what you remember defines who you are; when you forget your life, you cease to be, even before your death.” In his glib way, Barnes captured a sentiment that most people broadly share: We’re walking résumés, sentient histories who constitute our sense of self based on versions of what we’ve been. When you’re cognitively compromised from disease or age or drugs or something else, people start to talk about you as though your very being has vanished. He’s not himself. That’s just the disease talking. We pronounce these words with the implication that a loved one’s true being is one unblemished by any bits of embarrassing neurodegeneration. This is also how the hypochondriac or depressive or amnesiac sees things. Amnesiacs use a lot of verbs to describe what has happened to their memory, and one of the most common, I’ve found, is obliterated . It’s a telling choice. To be obliterated is to be erased, removed from any experience describable in letters. How, then, do we rewrite ourselves? M y time On the ward was short—just six days—but my course of ECT was long. I initially received nine treatments of the unilateral variety, with electrodes placed on my right temple. But my friends and family didn’t notice any improvement until I began thrice-weekly bilateral treatments. Bilateral can be more effective for some patients but is also more liable to complicate memory. When the bilateral treatments started to work, my friends saw it before I did—maybe because the only thing I noticed, for a while, was a deepening alienation from a full recollection of my self. Before long, though, I could talk with my sister on the phone in complete sentences, sometimes even long ones. My appetite began to reawaken. I could cook, after a fashion. I could sit at the piano and make it through a whole Ray Charles song. Yet the clearer my mind became, the more acutely I perceived the gaps. It’s particularly strange to encounter the absence of memory while you’re recovering your wits. “Looking at old pieces I wrote,” I noted in a fragmented journal entry, “I feel like an alien. I don’t know the guy who did any of this.” A psychiatrist told me I should fill these weeks of recovery with all of the things that I loved. “But I don’t love any of the old things,” I wrote. I’d always been pleased with my memory and considered it one of my main virtues. In the past, I’d been known as a steel trap or, as one ex-girlfriend put it, an “archivist,” often the first to remember a line of conversation or what stage the moon had been in during a night on the beach four summers ago. Now I had trouble remembering which beach I had gone to under said full moon. And when I pictured the woman I’d been with, I worried I was thinking of the wrong person. Who was I, really, without my memory parlor tricks? A troubled friend observed: “It’s like seeing an athlete you admire who all of a sudden can’t walk.” The good news was that, as bilateral treatments continued, my mood kept getting better. My personality, for good or ill, began to return. But certain memories did not. So I called Harold Sackeim, one of the greatest living authorities on ECT, to see whether he could tell me something about ECT, about myself; I wanted to pick his brain because I was scared and tired of picking my own. One of the things that has long intrigued him about the treatment, he told me, is that “it’s a laboratory for learning and memory.” Although some ECT researchers have described the memory effects as minimal or even nonexistent, Sackeim was up-front about them. Even decades ago, he said, he was warning patients that ECT can have permanent consequences. He was quick to add that these tend to be worth it: “I’ve never seen a patient with catatonia that didn’t get better.” Sackeim also stressed the neural benefits that can come with the treatment. “Tons of cognitive functions improve dramatically with ECT. Basically, when you’re depressed, it’s really hard to learn new things,” he said. “You’re so distracted by the things you’re either worrying about, or you’re agitated, pacing. And so you take in very little information about the world.” Finally, I asked him whether I should expect memories to return. He was admirably direct—didn’t hem or haw like most other doctors I’d asked. “What I tell people is that if some things don’t come back at six months, they’re never coming back.” W ith each day , I recognized new gaps: profound (when my girlfriend and I had first exchanged I love you ), frivolous (what I’d done the previous New Year’s Eve), and logistical (which of my mother’s knees had most recently undergone surgery). Right before my first ECT, I’d finished reading War and Peace , and six weeks later, all I could recall of the book was that Pierre was a gentle soul, and that moneyed Russians during the Napoleonic era ate lots of tasty French food. Even older memories seemed to be affected, some going as far back as 12 months. Of course, I knew basic facts about myself. But that’s very different from having direct access to your full memory—different, too, from identifying with your past, or with the illusion that any of it belonged to you. The doctors say that procedural memory isn’t affected in the same way as episodic memory. For example, ECT can rob you of a month of your life, but it’s essentially impossible that it will rob you of your ability to ride a bike. So I became greedy for procedural memory. Like a hoarder, I collected and cached away new skills to tether me to something firm. Lifting weights, I worked to rediscover what trainers refer to as the “mind-muscle connection,” and I kept putting on more muscle, a shield against future illness and general decrepitude. (In my deepest depression, I could hardly walk. A single kettlebell throw would’ve been as unimaginable as an ultramarathon.) But most of my caching took the form of accomplishments—slide guitar, jazz piano, anything with a learning curve. I taught myself to conjure the iridescent beauty of Billy Strayhorn’s “Lush Life” and the strutting octaves of George Gershwin’s “Rhapsody in Blue.” Once I trusted myself in public, I even began to play live music again, occasionally manning the keyboards in a friend’s country band. If my memory should encounter any future shock, I hoped, maybe this ever richer library of tricks could help bring me back. I also returned to the English and Latin texts that used to make me laugh in college and grad school. Rereading Fitzgerald, then Dickens, then Horace, then the always-hilarious Petronius, I began to remember all of the people I’d been when I first encountered these books. A further small but important bit of myself returned when I marshaled some of this reading into a long essay, about Petronius’s unlikely lessons for staying sane in a mad world. In the essay, I made my first public admission of having had ECT. Friends and strangers began to email me, and the emails read like whispers: “My mother got electroshock, but never wanted to admit it to anyone.” “My sister is beginning ECT. Is it ok if she emails you?” As I read the warm responses to the essay, I felt a noticeable lightening, a reprieve, as if I’d been exonerated from a murder charge: The alleged victim has walked into the courtroom, head held high, reciting Petronius. I was a new man, but I was the same ridiculous figure I’d always been. I was, in a sense, free. [ From the September 2026 issue: What if Freud was right? ] My dad, who sympathized with my memory challenges, recommended a book by the British psychologist Charles Fernyhough. It’s called Pieces of Light: How the New Science of Memory Illuminates the Stories We Tell About Our Pasts , and if you happen to have a memory disorder, reading Fernyhough is invigorating. As a scholar and humanist, he shows a deep understanding of amnesiacs, who “are caught between two identities, without the ability really to inhabit either.” He says we can look for hope in the associative nature of memory. Each memory exists as a network, drawing from various parts of the brain to constitute and reconstitute itself. In depression, those networks begin to fray. But just as associative memories thrive when activated internally, they can be stirred by external stimulation—“in collaboration” with others. Memory, Fernyhough observes, is “a social process.” Talking with my friend Brian brings up all sorts of little things I never would’ve expected: the time I met his daughter in our friend Aaron’s backyard, and the mischievous way she kept trying to pull the hood off my jacket. Talking with my friend Lucia takes me back to old, sad afternoons with her, in the garden outside my apartment, and how one songbird sounded so indignant. “Memory is not just about remembering the past or predicting the future,” Fernyhough writes. “It is also a way of being with other people. If you lose memory, you lose that opportunity to connect.” I now think of a compromised memory as a static page and a healthy memory as one with hyperlinks, richly connecting the full index of one’s past with the present through invisible threads of logic and fellowship. Socializing is the shortest path to remembering and the surest way to reestablish your sane, functional self. Sackeim once mentioned to me that depressives with strong kinship circles are much less likely to relapse or harm themselves than more isolated patients. Recovering your ability to joke, to act, to help is the single greatest thing you can do to restore personality and memory and joy. Perhaps the most important new memory is the one I created a week after my last maintenance ECT. I drove to visit my sister in Boston and met my nephew, Theo, in person for the first time. On Jane’s couch, this jowly 10-month-old and I sat face-to-face and inspected each other. Theo didn’t have any of the forbidding aspect he’d worn in my crayon drawing from the ward. After surveying me gravely, he reached out his hand with deliberate assurance and tried to remove my nose. Jane wept. There had been a time when she thought I’d never get to meet him. This article was adapted from Ted Scheinman’s new book, Jolt: My Electric Journey Out of Darkness .

items.title: UK Expands Human Rights Sanctions Regime
items.description: Click to expand Image Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband making a statement on Israel-Palestine in the House of Commons, London, United Kingdom, September 8, 2026. © 2026 Press Association via AP Photo The UK has significantly expanded its Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime, allowing the government, for the first time, to impose targeted sanctions on individuals and entities involved in war crimes. The new powers were approved by parliament yesterday. The previous framework, adopted in 2020, did not allow for such sanctions, providing, instead, for targeted sanctions only for certain serious human rights violations of the right to life, freedom from torture, and freedom from slavery and forced labor. Under the new rules, the government can also target those responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law, obstruction of humanitarian assistance, and violations of the right to liberty and security of person. This is an important step that means the UK can impose consequences for atrocities committed around the world. Although Foreign Secretary, Ed Miliband, announced the change in September while laying out measures to address Israel’s unlawful settlement expansion in the West Bank, the powers can also be used against those responsible for war crimes anywhere. Human Rights Watch has documented serious violations of international humanitarian law across the globe and called on governments to investigate individuals and entities with a view to imposing targeted sanctions. It is important that such sanctions are treated distinctly from criminal accountability. Sanctions should be used on those responsible for ongoing atrocities with the aim of bringing abuses to an end, and the UK should ensure that all persons affected by sanctions have due process rights to challenge them. Additionally, accountability for international criminal acts, past or present, should be implemented through criminal justice, including fair trials. In the West Bank, we documented the forced displacement of 32,000 Palestinians from three refugee camps in 2025, amounting to war crimes and crimes against humanity and called for targeted sanctions on officials including Defense Minister Israel Katz and Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth as well as criminal accountability. In Sudan, we found that the Abu Dhabi-based Global Security Services Group (GSSG), owned and run by Mohamed Hamdan al-Zaabi, apparently hired Colombian military contractors deployed to fight alongside the Rapid Support Forces, including in El Fasher, where the RSF committed mass atrocities. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the M23 and Rwandan Forces forcibly recruited and detained thousands, including children, subjecting them to horrific abuse in “training” camps for which Rwanda Defense Force Special Force Commander Stanislas Gashugi and M23 commanders Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Masozera were responsible. The new powers give the UK the tools to act against all the above individuals and entities. To ensure the credibility of its expanded regime, the UK should use it in a principled and consistent manner, imposing targeted sanctions where appropriate to help end atrocities. It should also ensure its criminal justice system can investigate and prosecute those responsible for war crimes, wherever they occur and whoever commits them.

items.title: Kébémer: 317 cas de diarrhées et de vomissements recensés en 72 heures
items.description: Depuis ce mardi, le département de Kébémer fait face à une situation sanitaire préoccupante. De nombreuses personnes souffrant de diarrhées et de vomissements se sont présentées au centre de santé de Kébémer. Au total, 317 cas ont été recensés en l’espace de 72 heures. Les patients continuent d’affluer vers la structure sanitaire, qui peine à faire face à cet afflux. Face à cette situation, les autorités sanitaires de la région de Louga se sont mobilisées. À cet effet, le directeur régional de la Santé, Dr Moustapha Faye, s’est rendu sur place pour s’enquérir de l’évolution de la situation. Une réunion d’urgence regroupant les autorités administratives et sanitaires est en cours afin de faire le point et d’examiner les mesures à prendre. Pour l’heure, les causes de ces nombreux cas de diarrhées et de vomissements restent inconnues. Toutefois, le personnel sanitaire est pleinement mobilisé pour déterminer l’origine de cette situation et prendre toutes les dispositions nécessaires afin d’endiguer la propagation de ces maladies. FALEL PAM

items.title: Equipe nationale : Pape Demba Diop, une première convocation qui récompense sa progression
items.description: Trois ans après avoir marqué la CAN U20 2023 de son empreinte avec cinq réalisations et un titre de meilleur buteur, le milieu de terrain de Strasbourg est récompensé par une première convocation en équipe nationale A. Pape Demba Diop franchit un nouveau cap dans sa carrière. Le milieu de terrain du Racing Club de Strasbourg figure parmi les 26 joueurs retenus par Patrick Vieira pour la double confrontation contre le Soudan, comptant pour les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. À 23 ans, le champion d’Afrique U20 de 2023 honore ainsi sa première convocation avec les Lions A. Cette sélection vient récompenser les prestations du milieu sénégalais, qui poursuit sa progression dans le football européen. Après avoir fait ses armes à Diambars, le natif de Ouakam a rejoint Zulte Waregem, en Belgique, où il s'est particulièrement illustré. Ses performances lui ont notamment permis de décrocher le titre de meilleur joueur de la Challenger Pro League lors de la saison 2024-2025. Il a ensuite rejoint Strasbourg avant de connaître un passage en Allemagne, puis un prêt à Toulouse. De retour en Alsace, Pape Demba Diop poursuit son parcours dans un championnat exigeant. Ses prestations avec le Racing ont convaincu le nouveau sélectionneur sénégalais de lui ouvrir les portes de la Tanière. Son arrivée dans le groupe national rappelle également de bons souvenirs aux supporters sénégalais. En 2023, lors de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations U20 disputée en Égypte, il avait formé un duo particulièrement performant avec Lamine Camara. Les deux milieux avaient largement contribué au sacre des Lionceaux, vainqueurs de la Gambie (2-0) en finale. Pape Demba Diop avait terminé la compétition avec cinq buts, s'adjugeant le titre de meilleur buteur, tandis que Lamine Camara avait été désigné meilleur joueur du tournoi. Trois ans après cette consécration, les deux anciens partenaires se retrouvent désormais chez les A. Face au Soudan, les 12 et 16 novembre prochains, Pape Demba Diop aura l'occasion de découvrir un nouvel environnement et de défendre ses chances sous le maillot national. Une étape importante pour celui qui, après avoir brillé avec les Lionceaux, aspire désormais à s'installer durablement parmi les Lions.
